scope: External authored question bank supplied via --bank-root; source records are not a live Firestore inventory.

workflow.production: One built-in image-generation call per reviewed item-specific prompt. No automatic runtime drawing.
workflow.review: Check exact values, angles, connections, arrows, labels, answer leakage and mobile readability before approval.
workflow.publishing: Require a passing question review and matching live stem; publish one approved asset using --only=<id> --diagram-only --apply.
workflow.resume: Reruns preserve requests, status, prompt and notes when the source hash matches. Changed questions return to brief-review.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: Two parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. At the first crossing point, one of the angles is 72°. Find the size of the corresponding angle at the second crossing point.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Kenji makes a model of the reaction between carbon and oxygen. He uses one black ball for a carbon atom, and two red balls joined together for an oxygen molecule. To show the product, carbon dioxide, he joins the black ball to the two red balls. Which of these does Kenji's model NOT show?
options: the number of each type of atom before and after the reaction
that the atoms are rearranged to make a new substance
that no atoms are made or lost in the reaction

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Ari makes a series circuit with one cell, a closed switch, a lamp and a buzzer. The lamp lights and the buzzer sounds. Then the thin wire inside the lamp breaks. What happens to the buzzer?
options: The buzzer stops, because the circuit is no longer complete.
The buzzer keeps working, because it is not part of the lamp.
The buzzer gets louder, because the lamp no longer uses the current.
The buzzer keeps working until the switch is opened.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The bearing of the school S from Dewi's house D is 237°. Find the bearing of D from S.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Kenji adds zinc granules to dilute sulfuric acid. He collects the hydrogen gas and records its total volume every 10 seconds. Results: at 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 s, the total volume of hydrogen is 0, 18, 32, 41, 46, 48 and 48 cm³. Mean rate of reaction = volume of gas ÷ time. Calculate the mean rate of reaction in the first 20 s.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A cell is connected to two lamps in parallel. Lamp 1 is in one branch and lamp 2 is in the other branch. An ammeter next to the cell, before the circuit splits, reads 0.8 A. An ammeter in the branch with lamp 1 reads 0.3 A. What is the current through lamp 2?

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: PQ and RS are parallel lines. A straight line crosses PQ at X and RS at Y. P and R are on the same side of the line XY. Angle PXY = \((3x + 10)^\circ\) and angle RYX = \((5x - 30)^\circ\). Find the size of angle PXY.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A sector of a circle has radius 12 cm and area 100 cm². Find the perimeter of the sector. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: In a titration, a student puts exactly 25.0 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide into a conical flask. The student then adds dilute hydrochloric acid until the indicator changes colour. The volume of acid added is recorded. Which row names the apparatus used to measure the alkali and to add the acid?
options: alkali: measuring cylinder; acid: volumetric pipette
alkali: volumetric pipette; acid: measuring cylinder

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student looks at some cells. The cells come from either a plant or an animal. Each cell has a cell wall, a cell membrane, a nucleus, cytoplasm, mitochondria and a large permanent vacuole. There are no chloroplasts. The student says the cells come from an animal, because they have no chloroplasts. Which statement is correct?
options: The student is correct, because all plant cells contain chloroplasts.
The cells are from a plant, because animal cells have no cell wall; not all plant cells have chloroplasts.
The cells are from a plant, because animal cells do not contain mitochondria.
The cells are from an animal, because they have a nucleus and a cell membrane.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Which statement describes the magnetic field lines around a bar magnet?
options: Outside the magnet, they go from the S pole to the N pole, and they never cross.
Outside the magnet, they go from the N pole to the S pole, and they never cross.
They point towards both poles of the magnet.
They cross each other near the poles, where the field is strongest.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student makes a series circuit with a cell, a lamp and two crocodile clips. There is a gap between the clips. She connects different materials across the gap. Which observation shows that a material is an electrical conductor?
options: The material is attracted to a magnet.
The material feels cold to touch.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The bearing of B from A is 125°. Find the bearing of A from B.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A car starts from rest. It speeds up at a constant rate, and then it travels at a constant speed. Which description of its speed–time graph is correct?
options: a horizontal line, then a straight line sloping upwards
a curve that gets steeper from the origin, then a horizontal line
a straight line sloping upwards from the origin, then a straight line sloping down to the time axis
a straight line sloping upwards from the origin, then a horizontal line

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A sector of a circle has radius 8 cm and angle 0.75 radians. Find the perimeter of the sector.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A car starts from rest and moves along a straight road with constant acceleration. Which description of its displacement–time graph is correct?
options: a straight line through the origin
a curve through the origin with a gradient that increases
a curve through the origin with a gradient that decreases

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The points A, B and C have coordinates \((1, 0, 2)\), \((3, -1, 4)\) and \((6, 2, 5)\). ABCD is a parallelogram, with the vertices in this order. O is the origin. Find the length of \(OD\).
jobs.authorBrief: A 3D-style sketch (not to scale) of a parallelogram with vertices A, B, C, D labelled in order going round the shape, so AB is parallel to DC and BC is parallel to AD. Label A (1, 0, 2), B (3, −1, 4), C (6, 2, 5); label D with the letter only (no coordinates). Show the origin O away from the parallelogram with a dashed line from O to D. Do not show any length.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
A student titrates 25.0 cm³ portions of aqueous sodium carbonate with dilute hydrochloric acid, using methyl orange indicator. Her titres are shown.
titration: rough, 1, 2, 3, 4
titre / cm³: 24.90, 24.30, 24.10, 24.65, 24.15
Which titres are concordant?

jobs.stem: A 3D shape has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices. Two of its faces are triangles. The other three faces are rectangles. Which shape is it?

jobs.subject: mathematics

options: a triangle on top of a rectangle
a circle on top of a rectangle
a triangle on top of a circle

jobs.stem: In a school canteen, square tables are put together in a row. One table seats 4 people. Two tables in a row seat 6 people. Three tables in a row seat 8 people. The pattern continues in the same way. Work out how many people can sit at 7 tables in a row.

The output is 38
Find the input.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A 3D shape has 12 vertices and 18 edges. Use Euler's formula to find the number of faces.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A triangular prism is 15 cm long. Its cross-section is a right-angled triangle with sides 6 cm, 8 cm and 10 cm. The two shorter sides, 6 cm and 8 cm, meet at the right angle. Calculate the total surface area of the prism.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: Which part of a plant cell is where photosynthesis happens?

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: What is the function of the cell membrane?
options: It gives the cell a fixed shape and support.
It controls what goes into and out of the cell.
It controls all the activities of the cell.

jobs.stem: Which description of the particles is correct for a gas?
options: close together, in a regular pattern, vibrating in fixed positions
close together, in no regular pattern, moving around each other
far apart, in no regular pattern, moving quickly in all directions
far apart, in a regular pattern, not moving

jobs.stem: Kenji does paper chromatography on a food colouring. The paper is 10.0 cm long. One spot moves 3.0 cm above the start line. The solvent moves 7.5 cm above the start line. Rf = distance moved by the spot ÷ distance moved by the solvent. Calculate the Rf value of the spot.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: Find the midpoint of the line segment joining A(2, 7) and B(8, −3).

jobs.stem: Triangle T has vertices (1, 1), (3, 1) and (1, 4). T is rotated 90° anticlockwise about (0, 0) to give triangle U. U is reflected in the x-axis to give triangle V. Which single transformation maps triangle T onto triangle V?

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A prism has a cross-section that is a trapezium. The parallel sides of the trapezium are 5 cm and 9 cm. The perpendicular distance between them is 4 cm. The length of the prism is 10 cm. Work out the volume of the prism.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A ray of light hits a plane mirror. The angle of incidence is 35°. What is the angle of reflection?

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Sound P and sound Q have the same frequency. The waveform of sound P has a larger amplitude than the waveform of sound Q. Which statement is correct?
options: Sound P has a higher pitch, and both sounds are equally loud.
Sound P is louder and has a higher pitch.
Sound P is quieter, and both sounds have the same pitch.
Sound P is louder, and both sounds have the same pitch.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Ari reacts marble chips with dilute hydrochloric acid. The reaction makes carbon dioxide gas. Which method can he use to measure the rate of this reaction?
options: Measure the volume of gas made every 30 seconds, using a gas syringe and a stop-watch.
Measure the temperature of the acid at the start, using a thermometer.
Measure the mass of the marble chips at the start only, using a balance.
Measure the volume of acid at the start, using a measuring cylinder.

jobs.stem: The parallel sides of a trapezium are 9 cm and 15 cm long. The perpendicular distance between them is 6 cm. Find the area of the trapezium.

jobs.stem: A cylinder has diameter 8 cm and height 10 cm. Find the volume of the cylinder. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A right-angled triangle has two shorter sides of length 7 cm and 10 cm. Find the length of the hypotenuse. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student measures the volume of hydrogen gas made in a reaction every 30 seconds. Which two pieces of apparatus does the student need?
options: a volumetric pipette and a stopwatch
a gas syringe and a stopwatch
a gas syringe and a thermometer

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Lena puts a spot of a purple food dye on the start line of a piece of chromatography paper. She uses water as the solvent. The start line is above the level of the water. When the water has moved near the top of the paper, the purple spot is still on the start line. Which explanation is correct?
options: The dye is insoluble in water, so a different solvent is needed.
The dye is a pure substance, so it does not move.
The dye is very soluble in water, so it stays on the start line.
The start line should have been below the level of the water.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: Which structures does a virus have?
options: a cell wall and a nucleus
a protein coat and genetic material

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: Which list contains only structures that are found in a bacterial cell?
options: cell wall, chloroplasts, cytoplasm, circular DNA
cell membrane, circular DNA, ribosomes, plasmids

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A muscle cell uses oxygen and produces carbon dioxide. Both gases move through its cell membrane by diffusion. Which row shows the direction in which each gas diffuses?
options: oxygen: into the cell; carbon dioxide: into the cell
oxygen: into the cell; carbon dioxide: out of the cell
oxygen: out of the cell; carbon dioxide: into the cell
oxygen: out of the cell; carbon dioxide: out of the cell

In a dot-and-cross diagram of phosphine, how many lone pairs (pairs of outer-shell electrons that are not shared) are on the phosphorus atom?

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A magnesium atom (electronic configuration 2,8,2) forms an ion with a full outer shell. Which row describes how the ion forms and what type of ion it is?

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A crate on ice is pulled by two ropes. One rope pulls with a force of 24 N due east. The other rope pulls with a force of 10 N due north. Which row gives the size of the resultant force and the angle between the resultant force and due east? Angles are given to the nearest degree.

jobs.subject: mathematics

jobs.stem: The points \(A(-1, 4)\) and \(B(5, -2)\) are the ends of a diameter of a circle. Find the equation of the circle.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Which statement describes the structure of an atom?
options: The protons, neutrons and electrons are spread evenly through the whole volume of the atom.
A large nucleus fills most of the atom, and the electrons are held inside the nucleus with the protons.
A very small, dense nucleus contains the protons and electrons; the neutrons are in shells around it.
A very small, dense nucleus contains the protons and neutrons; the electrons are in shells in the mostly empty space around it.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Two forces act on the same point. One force is 9.0 N towards the east. The other force is 4.0 N towards the north. Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force, to 2 significant figures.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A rope pulls a box with a force of 50 N at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Calculate the horizontal component of this force, to 2 significant figures.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Two 10 kΩ resistors are connected in series to a 12 V supply of negligible internal resistance. A voltmeter of resistance 10 kΩ is connected across one of the resistors. Calculate the reading on the voltmeter.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: Angle \(A\) is acute and \(\sin A = \frac{8}{17}\). Angle \(B\) is obtuse and \(\cos B = -\frac{5}{13}\). Find the exact value of \(\cos(A - B)\).

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
A student adds 0.5 g of manganese(IV) oxide to 20 cm³ of dilute aqueous hydrogen peroxide in a conical flask connected to a 100 cm³ gas syringe. In a trial run, oxygen is given off quickly at first, and the volume stops changing after about 80 s, at about 70 cm³.
She wants to plot a graph of volume of oxygen against time and use it to find the initial rate.
Which plan collects an appropriate quantity of data?
options: Read the volume every 60 s from 0 s to 300 s.
Read the volume once, at 300 s.
Read the volume every 10 s from 0 s to 40 s.
Read the volume every 10 s from 0 s to 150 s.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view on a bench: conical flask labelled "aqueous hydrogen peroxide" with a small heap of black powder labelled "manganese(IV) oxide"; bung with a delivery tube leading to a horizontal 100 cm³ gas syringe, scale 0 to 100 cm³ marked every 10 cm³, plunger at 0. No time readings or graph.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The graph of \(y = |2x-4|\) is V-shaped, with its vertex on the \(x\)-axis. A straight line passes through the point \((0, 1)\) and has gradient \(m\), so its equation is \(y = mx+1\). Find the set of values of \(m\) for which the line meets the graph of \(y = |2x-4|\) at exactly two points.
jobs.authorBrief: x from −1 to 5, y from −1 to 6. Draw y = |2x − 4| as two straight arms meeting on the x-axis; label the y-intercept (0, 4) and the vertex (2, 0). Mark and label the point (0, 1). Do not draw any line through (0, 1).

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The variables \(x\) and \(y\) satisfy the equation \(y = Ax^n\), where \(A\) and \(n\) are constants. The graph of \(\ln y\) against \(\ln x\) is a straight line through the points \((0.8, 2.9)\) and \((2.3, 6.2)\). Find the values of \(n\) and \(A\), giving \(A\) correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Horizontal axis ln x from 0 to 3, vertical axis ln y from 0 to 7. Draw a straight line through the marked points (0.8, 2.9) and (2.3, 6.2), each labelled with its coordinates. Extend the line to the vertical axis but do not label the intercept value.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The region R is bounded by the curve \(y = 4 - e^{2x}\), the x-axis and the y-axis. Find the exact area of R.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x and y with origin O. Draw y = 4 − e^(2x) for x from about −0.3 to 0.9, decreasing, meeting the y-axis at (0, 3) (label 3) and crossing the positive x-axis. Shade the region R bounded by the curve, the x-axis and the y-axis and label it R. Do not label the x-coordinate where the curve crosses the x-axis.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The region R lies between the curve \(y = 3\sin\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)\) and the x-axis, from the y-axis to the point where the curve first meets the positive x-axis. Find the exact area of R.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x and y with origin O. Draw y = 3 sin(2x + π/6) from x = 0 to a little past the point where it first meets the positive x-axis: it starts at (0, 1.5) on the y-axis (label 1.5), rises to a maximum of 3 and falls to the x-axis. Shade the region R between the curve, the y-axis and the x-axis and label it R. Do not mark the x-coordinate where the curve meets the x-axis or the x-coordinate of the maximum.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: Use the trapezium rule with 4 intervals to estimate the value of \(\int_0^2 \sqrt{1 + x^3}\,dx\). Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x and y. Draw y = √(1 + x³) from x = 0 (y = 1) to x = 2 (y = 3). Mark x = 0, 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 on the x-axis and draw vertical lines up to the curve at each. Join the tops of neighbouring lines with straight segments to show four trapezia. Do not write the heights of the inner ordinates or any area.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The curve \(y = (x - 4)\ln x\), for \(x > 0\), has one stationary point. Its \(x\)-coordinate is \(\alpha\). Which iterative formula comes from a correct rearrangement of the equation that \(\alpha\) satisfies?
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x from 0 to 6, y from −2 to 4. Draw y = (x − 4) ln x for x > 0: it comes down from above the top of the window near x = 0, crosses the x-axis at (1, 0), reaches one minimum point, rises to cross the x-axis again at (4, 0) and keeps rising. Mark the minimum point with a dot and the label "x = α" on the x-axis below it. Do not print a numerical value for α.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The curves \(y = \mathrm{e}^{\frac{x}{2}}\) and \(y = 6 - x^2\) meet at the point P, which has a positive \(x\)-coordinate \(\alpha\). The sequence given by \(x_{n+1} = \sqrt{6 - \mathrm{e}^{\frac{x_n}{2}}}\), with \(x_1 = 2\), converges to \(\alpha\). Use this iteration to find \(\alpha\) correct to 3 decimal places. Hence find the gradient of the curve \(y = \mathrm{e}^{\frac{x}{2}}\) at P, correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x from −3 to 3, y from −3 to 7. Draw the increasing exponential curve y = e^(x/2) through (0, 1) and the parabola y = 6 − x² with vertex (0, 6). Mark the intersection with positive x-coordinate as P and write "x = α" on the x-axis below it. The second intersection (negative x) is shown but not labelled. No numerical value for α and no tangent line.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The complex number \(z\) satisfies \(|z - 4 - 4i| = 2\). Find the greatest value of \(\arg z\). Give your answer in radians correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Argand diagram with labelled Re and Im axes and origin O, both axes marked 0 to 7. Draw the circle with centre C at (4, 4) and radius 2; label the centre "4 + 4i" and mark the radius 2. Do not draw tangents from O or any angle, and do not mark any point of the circle other than the centre.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A robot moves along a straight corridor. Its displacement s metres from a fixed point at time t seconds is shown by a graph made of straight-line segments joining these points, in order: (t = 0, s = 0), (t = 10, s = 40), (t = 16, s = 40), (t = 26, s = −10). Find the velocity of the robot during the last stage, from t = 16 s to t = 26 s.
jobs.authorBrief: Displacement–time graph: horizontal axis t (s) from 0 to 28, vertical axis s (m) from −15 to 45, with the t-axis at s = 0. Plot and join with straight lines the points (0, 0), (10, 40), (16, 40) and (26, −10). Label the axes "t (s)" and "s (m)". No gradients or velocities written on the graph.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A runner moves along a straight path. Her displacement s metres from a starting line at time t seconds is shown by a graph made of straight-line segments joining these points, in order: (t = 0, s = 0), (t = 5, s = 30), (t = 12, s = 30), (t = 20, s = −18), (t = 25, s = −8). Find her average speed for the 25 seconds. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Displacement–time graph: horizontal axis t (s) from 0 to 26, vertical axis s (m) from −20 to 35, with the t-axis at s = 0. Plot and join with straight lines the points (0, 0), (5, 30), (12, 30), (20, −18) and (25, −8). Label the axes "t (s)" and "s (m)". No distances, gradients or speeds written on the graph.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A tram travels along a straight track between two stops. It starts from rest and accelerates uniformly for 40 s to a speed of V m s⁻¹. It then moves at this constant speed for 180 s. Finally it decelerates uniformly for 60 s and comes to rest at the second stop. The distance between the stops is 5520 m. Find V.
jobs.authorBrief: Velocity–time graph: horizontal axis t (s), vertical axis v (m s⁻¹). Straight line from (0, 0) up to (40, V), horizontal line from (40, V) to (220, V), straight line down to (280, 0). Mark the times 40, 220 and 280 on the t-axis and the label V on the v-axis. Do not give a value for V or the distance.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A particle starts from the point O at time t = 0 seconds and moves in a straight line. Its velocity–time graph is made of straight-line segments joining these points, in order: (t = 0, v = 6), (t = 4, v = −2), (t = 10, v = −2), (t = 12, v = 0), where v m s⁻¹ is the velocity at time t seconds. Find the value of t, with t > 0, when the particle is first back at O.
jobs.authorBrief: Velocity–time graph: horizontal axis t (s) from 0 to 13, vertical axis v (m s⁻¹) from −3 to 7, with the t-axis at v = 0. Plot and join with straight lines the points (0, 6), (4, −2), (10, −2) and (12, 0). Label the axes "t (s)" and "v (m s⁻¹)". Do not mark where the graph crosses the t-axis and do not shade any areas.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A ball is released from rest above a horizontal floor. It hits the floor at \(t = 0.8\) and bounces. The velocity-time graph of the ball, with upwards taken as positive, is described below. Time \(t\) is in seconds and velocity \(v\) is in \(\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). From \(t = 0\) to \(t = 0.8\) the graph is a straight line from \((0, 0)\) to \((0.8, -8)\). At \(t = 0.8\) the velocity jumps to \(+5\). From \(t = 0.8\) to \(t = 1.8\) the graph is a straight line from \((0.8, 5)\) to \((1.8, -5)\). Find the height of the ball above the floor at \(t = 1.6\).
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: time t in s from 0 to 1.8 (horizontal), velocity v in m/s from -8 to 5 (vertical, upwards positive). Straight segment from (0, 0) to (0.8, -8). Vertical jump at t = 0.8 (filled dot at (0.8, -8), open dot at (0.8, 5) or a dashed vertical line). Straight segment from (0.8, 5) to (1.8, -5). Mark t = 1.6 on the time axis with a tick only. No shaded areas, no heights written.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A barge of mass 800 kg is pulled along a straight canal by two horizontal ropes, one from each bank. One rope has tension 300 N and makes an angle of \(20^\circ\) with the direction of the canal. The other rope makes an angle of \(35^\circ\) with the direction of the canal, on the other side. The barge moves along the canal, so the resultant force has no component across the canal. A resistance of 250 N acts against the motion. Find the acceleration of the barge. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Plan view. Two parallel lines for the canal banks, a small barge in the middle. Arrow showing the direction of the canal (direction of motion). Rope to one bank labelled 300 N, angle 20° marked between the rope and the canal direction. Rope to the other bank labelled T, angle 35° marked between the rope and the canal direction. Arrow opposite the motion labelled 250 N resistance. Do not show any resultant or the value of T.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A small ring rests on a smooth horizontal table. Four horizontal strings pull the ring, and it stays in equilibrium. Three of the forces are: 12 N towards the east; 5 N towards the north; 9 N in the direction \(40^\circ\) south of west. Find the magnitude and direction of the fourth force, P.
jobs.authorBrief: Plan view with a compass mark (N up, E right). Ring at the centre. Arrow to the east labelled 12 N. Arrow to the north labelled 5 N. Arrow pointing between west and south labelled 9 N, with the angle 40° marked between it and the west direction. A fourth arrow labelled P drawn in a neutral direction (for example straight up-left at a vague angle) with no angle marked; or omit the P arrow and write "fourth force P".

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A cart of mass 8 kg is held at rest on a smooth straight track inclined at angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\tan\alpha = \frac{3}{4}\). It is held by a light rope. The rope pulls up the slope. It is above the track, in the vertical plane of the track, and makes an angle of \(15^\circ\) with the track. Take \(g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find the tension in the rope. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view. Straight track inclined at angle α to the horizontal (angle marked α at the bottom). A small cart on the track. A rope from the cart going up the slope, drawn above the track and making an angle of 15° with the track (angle marked). Label the cart 8 kg. Do not draw force arrows with values.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The continuous random variable \(X\) has probability density function \(f\) given by \(f(x) = \frac{2}{x^2}\) for \(1 \le x \le 2\), and \(f(x) = 0\) otherwise. Find the exact value of \(\mathrm{P}(X > 1.5)\).
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x from 0 to 2.5 and f(x) from 0 to 2.2. Draw the curve y = 2/x² from (1, 2) to (2, 0.5), with f(x) = 0 on the x-axis for x < 1 and x > 2, and thin dashed vertical lines at x = 1 and x = 2. Mark x = 1.5 on the x-axis. No shading and no area values.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: The continuous random variable \(X\) has probability density function \(f\) given by \(f(x) = \frac{x}{2}\) for \(0 \le x \le 1\), \(f(x) = \frac{4 - x}{6}\) for \(1 \lt x \le 4\), and \(f(x) = 0\) otherwise. Find the exact value of the median of \(X\).
jobs.authorBrief: Axes x from 0 to 4.5 and f(x) from 0 to 0.6. Draw the line segment from (0, 0) to (1, 0.5) labelled f(x) = x/2, and the line segment from (1, 0.5) to (4, 0) labelled f(x) = (4 − x)/6. Mark 1, 2, 3, 4 on the x-axis and 0.5 on the f(x)-axis. Do not mark the median or any area.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A crate of mass 25 kg is pulled up a slope inclined at \(12^\circ\) to the horizontal by a rope. The rope makes an angle of \(20^\circ\) with a line of greatest slope, above the slope. A constant resistance of 60 N acts down the slope. The crate moves up the line of greatest slope with acceleration \(0.4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Take \(g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find the tension in the rope. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view. Slope inclined at 12° to the horizontal (angle marked). Crate on the slope labelled 25 kg. Rope from the crate going up the slope, above the line of greatest slope, angle 20° marked between rope and slope. Arrow down the slope labelled resistance 60 N. Arrow up the slope labelled a = 0.4 m/s². No tension value.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: Particle \(A\) of mass 3 kg lies on a rough horizontal table. The coefficient of friction between \(A\) and the table is \(0.25\). A light inextensible string joins \(A\) to particle \(B\) of mass 2 kg. The string passes over a small smooth pulley fixed at the edge of the table, and \(B\) hangs freely below the pulley. The system is released from rest with the string taut. Take \(g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find the tension in the string while the particles move.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view: horizontal table top; block A (label "A, 3 kg") on the table; a straight horizontal string from A to a small pulley fixed at the right-hand edge of the table; the string then hangs vertically to block B (label "B, 2 kg"). Mark the table surface "rough". No forces or arrows.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: Particle \(A\) of mass 4 kg lies on a smooth plane inclined at angle \(\alpha\) to the horizontal, where \(\sin\alpha = 0.6\). A light inextensible string, parallel to a line of greatest slope, joins \(A\) to particle \(B\) of mass 6 kg. The string passes over a small smooth pulley at the top of the plane, and \(B\) hangs 1.5 m above horizontal ground. The system is released from rest with the string taut. \(B\) hits the ground and does not bounce. \(A\) never reaches the pulley. Take \(g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find the total distance that \(A\) moves up the plane from the moment of release until it first comes to instantaneous rest.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view: a plane inclined at angle α to the horizontal ground, with a small pulley at its top. Particle A (label "A, 4 kg") on the slope; the string runs from A parallel to the slope up to the pulley and then hangs vertically to particle B (label "B, 6 kg"). Mark the vertical distance from B down to the ground as "1.5 m". Label the angle α and write "sin α = 0.6". No forces or arrows.

jobs.subject: mathematics
jobs.stem: A smooth hemispherical bowl of radius 0.8 m is fixed with its rim horizontal. A small particle is released from rest on the inside surface, at the rim. Later the particle passes a point \(P\) on the inside surface. The radius from the centre of the rim to \(P\) makes an angle of \(30^\circ\) with the vertical. Take \(g = 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\). Find the speed of the particle at \(P\). Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Vertical cross-section of a hemispherical bowl, rim horizontal at the top; mark the centre O of the rim. Draw a dashed vertical line down from O and a radius from O to a point P on the inside surface, with the angle between the radius OP and the vertical marked 30°. Label the radius "0.8 m". Show a small particle starting at one end of the rim. Do not draw any heights.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A chemist wants to make 2-hydroxy-3-methylbutanoic acid, (CH3)2CHCH(OH)COOH, in two steps. Step 1: a carbonyl compound is converted into a hydroxynitrile. Step 2: the –CN group of the hydroxynitrile is converted into a –COOH group. Which carbonyl compound is used in step 1?
jobs.authorBrief: Three boxes in a row joined by arrows. Box 1: "carbonyl compound ?". Arrow 1 labelled only "step 1". Box 2: "hydroxynitrile". Arrow 2 labelled only "step 2". Box 3: the displayed formula of 2-hydroxy-3-methylbutanoic acid, (CH3)2CHCH(OH)COOH, with its name underneath. Draw no structure in box 1 or box 2, and write no reagents or conditions on the arrows.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound Y has the molecular formula C3H6O. Its infrared spectrum shows a broad absorption centred at 3350 cm⁻¹, a medium absorption at 1645 cm⁻¹ and a strong absorption at 1050 cm⁻¹. There is no absorption between 1670 and 1740 cm⁻¹. Data: C–O (alcohols, ethers, esters) 1040–1300 cm⁻¹; C=C (alkenes) 1500–1680 cm⁻¹; C=O (aldehydes, ketones) 1670–1740 cm⁻¹; O–H (alcohols, hydrogen bonded, broad) 3200–3600 cm⁻¹. Which compound could Y be?
options: cyclopropanol, a three-membered carbon ring with one OH group
jobs.authorBrief: IR spectrum, x-axis "wavenumber / cm⁻¹" from 4000 (left) to 500 (right), y-axis "transmittance / %" from 0 to 100. Draw: a broad, deep, rounded absorption from about 3200 to 3500 centred at 3350; small sharp C–H absorptions between 2850 and 3100; a medium sharp absorption at 1645; a strong sharp absorption at 1050; a flat baseline from 1670 to 1740 with no absorption; minor fingerprint peaks below 1000. Label only the axes; do not label any peak with a bond or a group.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
A student measures the starting temperature of 25 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide in a plastic cup. The thermometer is marked at 1 °C intervals. The top of the liquid in the thermometer is between the 23 °C and 24 °C marks, about one-third of the way from 23 °C to 24 °C.
Which value should the student record?
jobs.authorBrief: Vertical section of a liquid-in-glass thermometer from 20 °C to 26 °C, a mark every 1 °C, each mark numbered. Draw the top of the liquid column one-third of the way from the 23 °C mark to the 24 °C mark. No written reading.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
A student electrolyses aqueous copper(II) sulfate using copper electrodes and a constant current. She uses a fresh, weighed cathode each time and records the increase in mass of the cathode after different times.
time / min: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50
increase in mass / g: 0.060, 0.119, 0.180, 0.205, 0.298
Which action should the student take next?
options: Repeat the 10 min experiment, because the smallest mass has the largest percentage uncertainty.
Change the 40 min result to 0.239 g so that it fits the trend.
Repeat the 50 min experiment, because it gives the largest increase in mass.
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis: time / min, 0 to 60, marked every 10. y-axis: increase in mass / g, 0 to 0.320, marked every 0.040. Plot small crosses at (10, 0.060), (20, 0.119), (30, 0.180), (40, 0.205), (50, 0.298). No line drawn and no point labelled.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student adds different volumes of aqueous sodium sulfate to separate portions of aqueous barium chloride. The barium chloride is always in excess. Each precipitate of barium sulfate is filtered, washed, dried and weighed. (Results: volume of sodium sulfate solution / cm³: 0.0, 5.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0, 25.0, 30.0; mass of barium sulfate / g: 0.000, 0.115, 0.236, 0.348, 0.395, 0.587, 0.698.) The student expects the mass of precipitate to be directly proportional to the volume of sodium sulfate solution. Which line should the student draw on a graph of mass of barium sulfate against volume of sodium sulfate solution?
options: a smooth curve that passes through every point, including the point at 20.0 cm³
a straight line through the origin with the other points spread evenly on both sides, and the point at 20.0 cm³ labelled as anomalous
a straight line pulled down towards the point at 20.0 cm³, so that most of the other points lie above it
short straight lines joining each point to the next point
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x-axis "volume of sodium sulfate solution / cm³" from 0 to 35; y-axis "mass of barium sulfate / g" from 0 to 0.800. Plot the seven points from the table as small crosses. Do not draw any line, and do not label or highlight any point.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student puts 25.0 cm³ of aqueous sodium hydroxide in a polystyrene cup and adds 1.50 mol dm⁻³ nitric acid from a burette, recording the temperature. (Results: volume of acid added / cm³: 0.00, 2.00, 4.00, 6.00, 8.00, 14.00, 16.00, 18.00, 20.00; temperature / °C: 21.0, 22.5, 24.0, 25.5, 27.0, 29.5, 29.0, 28.5, 28.0.) The student draws one straight line of best fit through the first five points and another through the last four points. The end-point is where the two lines meet. What is the concentration of the sodium hydroxide, to 3 significant figures?
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x-axis "volume of nitric acid added / cm³" from 0 to 20; y-axis "temperature / °C" from 20 to 32. Plot the nine readings from the table as small crosses. Do not draw the lines of best fit and do not mark where they meet.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student measures the temperature of 50.0 cm³ of aqueous copper(II) sulfate in a polystyrene cup every 0.5 min. At 2.5 min an excess of zinc powder is added and the mixture is stirred; no reading is taken at 2.5 min or 3.0 min. Results: time / min: 0.0 to 2.0, temperature 24.0 °C at every reading; then (time, temperature) 3.5, 44.0; 4.0, 43.5; 4.5, 43.0; 5.0, 42.5; 5.5, 42.0; 6.0, 41.5 °C. The readings from 3.5 min fall on a straight line. The student extrapolates this line to find the temperature rise at the moment of mixing. What is the temperature rise?
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x-axis "time / min" from 0 to 6.0; y-axis "temperature / °C" from 20 to 50. Plot the eleven temperature readings from the table as small crosses. Draw a short vertical dashed line at 2.5 min labelled "zinc added". Do not draw any line of best fit or extrapolated line.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Dilute sulfuric acid is electrolysed with inert electrodes and a current of 0.800 A. The electrode reactions are 2H+(aq) + 2e− → H2(g) and 2H2O(l) → O2(g) + 4H+(aq) + 4e−. Both gases are collected in one container. How long does it take to collect a total of 60.0 cm³ of gas, measured at room conditions? F = 9.65 × 10⁴ C mol⁻¹; molar gas volume at room conditions = 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹. Assume no gas dissolves. Give the answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Beaker of dilute sulfuric acid with two inert electrodes (labelled electrode 1 and electrode 2, not cathode/anode). Wires to a d.c. power supply with an ammeter reading 0.800 A in the circuit. A funnel or two delivery tubes above the electrodes lead gas into a single inverted measuring cylinder over water, labelled "total volume of gas". No numbers other than the current; no gas names on the figure.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A constant current of I amperes is passed for t seconds through aqueous copper(II) sulfate between two copper electrodes. The anode loses m1 grams and the cathode gains m2 grams. m1 is a little larger than m2 because some small pieces of copper fall off the anode during the experiment. The relative atomic mass of copper is A and the charge on one electron is e coulombs. Which expression gives a correct value of the Avogadro constant, L?
jobs.authorBrief: Beaker of aqueous copper(II) sulfate with two copper plate electrodes, labelled anode and cathode. Circuit: d.c. power supply, ammeter, variable resistor and switch in series with the cell. A few small fragments of copper drawn on the bottom of the beaker below the anode. A stop-clock beside the circuit. No numerical values.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: To measure the standard electrode potential of the Pb2+/Pb half-cell, a lead electrode in aqueous lead(II) nitrate is connected to a reference half-cell by a salt bridge and a voltmeter. Which salt bridge is suitable, and why?
options: filter paper soaked in aqueous sodium sulfate, because sulfate ions are not oxidised or reduced at either electrode
a platinum wire, because platinum is inert and lets electrons flow between the two solutions
filter paper soaked in aqueous potassium nitrate, because it lets electrons flow between the two solutions
filter paper soaked in aqueous potassium nitrate, because its ions complete the circuit and do not form a precipitate with Pb²⁺
jobs.authorBrief: Left beaker: lead rod in aqueous lead(II) nitrate. Right beaker: an electrode in a solution, labelled only "reference half-cell". A voltmeter joins the two electrodes by wires. A U-shaped strip between the beakers labelled only "salt bridge" — do not show or name what it is soaked in.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A cell is made from a Mn2+/Mn half-cell and a Ni2+/Ni half-cell under standard conditions. E⦵ values: Mn2+(aq) + 2e− ⇌ Mn(s), −1.18 V; Ni2+(aq) + 2e− ⇌ Ni(s), −0.25 V. Which row gives the negative electrode and the direction of electron flow in the external circuit?
jobs.authorBrief: Left beaker: manganese strip in Mn2+(aq). Right beaker: nickel strip in Ni2+(aq). A wire through a voltmeter joins the two strips; a salt bridge joins the solutions. No + or − signs and no arrows on the wire.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A cell is made from a Zn²⁺/Zn half-cell and a Cl2/Cl⁻ half-cell. The Cl2/Cl⁻ half-cell has chlorine gas bubbling over a platinum electrode in aqueous chloride ions. The half-cells are joined by a salt bridge. E⦵(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V and E⦵(Cl2/Cl⁻) = +1.36 V. Which single change makes the cell e.m.f. smaller?
options: decreasing the concentration of \(\mathrm{Zn^{2+}(aq)}\) in the zinc half-cell
increasing the pressure of \(\mathrm{Cl_2(g)}\) in the chlorine half-cell
using a platinum electrode with a larger surface area
increasing the concentration of \(\mathrm{Cl^-(aq)}\) in the chlorine half-cell
jobs.authorBrief: Left beaker: zinc rod dipping into Zn²⁺(aq), labelled "Zn²⁺(aq)". Right beaker: platinum electrode dipping into Cl⁻(aq), with a glass tube delivering Cl2(g) bubbling over the platinum, labelled "Cl2(g)" and "Cl⁻(aq)". A salt bridge joins the two solutions; wires from both electrodes go to a high-resistance voltmeter (V). Do not mark which electrode is positive or negative.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound Y is shaken with 50.0 cm³ of hexane and 100 cm³ of water in a separating funnel at 25 °C until equilibrium is reached. The hexane layer then contains 0.800 g of Y and the water layer contains 0.200 g of Y. Calculate the partition coefficient, Kpc, of Y between hexane and water, with hexane on the top of the ratio.
jobs.authorBrief: A stoppered separating funnel with a closed tap, clamped upright. Upper layer labelled "hexane, 50.0 cm³, contains 0.800 g of Y"; lower layer labelled "water, 100 cm³, contains 0.200 g of Y". A clear boundary between the layers. No other labels or calculations.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound G decomposes at constant temperature. Readings of [G] were taken: at 0 s, 0.900 mol dm⁻³; at 60 s, 0.750 mol dm⁻³; at 120 s, 0.600 mol dm⁻³; at 180 s, 0.450 mol dm⁻³; at 240 s, 0.300 mol dm⁻³. Which row gives the order of reaction with respect to G and the shape of a graph of rate against [G]?
options: order 0; a straight line through the origin
order 1; a straight line through the origin
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x = time / s from 0 to 240; y = [G] / mol dm⁻³ from 0 to 1.000. Plot the five readings (0, 0.900), (60, 0.750), (120, 0.600), (180, 0.450), (240, 0.300) as crosses. No line of best fit, no gradient or half-life marks, and no label naming the order.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: J and K react at constant temperature. In a set of initial-rate experiments, a graph of initial rate against [J] is a curve through the origin that gets steeper as [J] increases, and a graph of initial rate against [J]² is a straight line through the origin. Changing [K] while [J] is kept constant has no effect on the initial rate. In one experiment, [J] = 0.050 mol dm⁻³, [K] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³ and the initial rate is 3.00 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. What is the initial rate when [J] = 0.075 mol dm⁻³ and [K] = 0.080 mol dm⁻³, to 3 significant figures?
jobs.authorBrief: Two small graphs side by side, no numbers needed. Left: y = initial rate / mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹, x = [J] / mol dm⁻³; a smooth curve that starts at the origin and gets steeper. Right: the same y-axis, x = [J]² / mol² dm⁻⁶; a straight line through the origin. Do not write the order or the rate equation on either graph.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A metal oxide, MO, can be reduced by carbon: MO(s) + C(s) → M(s) + CO(g). The table shows ΔG⦵ for this reaction at four temperatures. ΔG⦵ / kJ mol⁻¹: +40 at 600 K, +12 at 800 K, −16 at 1000 K, −44 at 1200 K. At which of these temperatures is the reduction feasible under standard conditions?
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis: temperature / K from 500 to 1300. y-axis: ΔG⦵ / kJ mol⁻¹ from −60 to +60, with the line ΔG⦵ = 0 drawn and labelled 0. Plot four points (600, +40), (800, +12), (1000, −16), (1200, −44) and join them with a straight line. Title: MO(s) + C(s) → M(s) + CO(g). Do not shade or label any region as feasible or not feasible.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Element X is a Period 4 element in the d block. Its first eight ionisation energies are: 717, 1509, 3248, 4940, 6990, 9220, 11 500 and 18 770 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the highest oxidation state that X is likely to show in its compounds?
jobs.authorBrief: Bar chart. x-axis: number of electrons removed, 1 to 8. y-axis: ionisation energy / kJ mol⁻¹ from 0 to 20 000, linear scale. Bar heights: 717, 1509, 3248, 4940, 6990, 9220, 11 500, 18 770, each value printed above its bar. No labels on sub-shells or shells.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A 1.50 g sample of brass (an alloy of copper and zinc) is dissolved in acid and the excess acid is neutralised. The solution is made up to 250.0 cm³. A 25.0 cm³ portion is added to excess aqueous potassium iodide: 2Cu²⁺ + 4I⁻ → I2 + 2CuI. The iodine formed reacts with 18.40 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ sodium thiosulfate: I2 + 2S2O3²⁻ → 2I⁻ + S4O6²⁻. Zinc ions do not react with iodide ions. Ar of Cu is 63.5 here. Calculate the percentage by mass of copper in the brass, to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Five boxes joined by arrows, left to right: (1) 1.50 g brass dissolved in acid, excess acid neutralised; (2) solution made up to 250.0 cm³ in a volumetric flask; (3) 25.0 cm³ portion removed with a pipette; (4) excess aqueous KI added — white precipitate in a brown solution; (5) titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ Na2S2O3, mean titre 18.40 cm³. No calculations or answers on the chart.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: The molecule dien, H2NCH2CH2NHCH2CH2NH2, has a lone pair on each of its three nitrogen atoms, and the chain is flexible enough for all three lone pairs to form dative bonds to the same metal ion. Dien molecules replace all six water ligands in [Mn(H2O)6]2+. Which row is correct? (Each option gives: the type of ligand that dien is; the number of dien molecules in the new complex.)
jobs.authorBrief: Draw the displayed formula of dien, H2N-CH2-CH2-NH-CH2-CH2-NH2, as a zig-zag chain. Show every C-H and N-H bond and draw one lone pair (two dots) on each of the three nitrogen atoms. Label the molecule "dien". Do not draw any metal ion, ligand count or the word bidentate/polydentate.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: The complex ion [Co(H2O)6]2+ is octahedral. Consider every possible pair of water ligands. How many of the O–Co–O bond angles are 90°?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw [Co(H2O)6]2+ as an octahedron: Co at the centre, two H2O ligands on the vertical axis and four in the horizontal plane (wedge and dashed bonds for perspective). Each ligand is bonded through O (write "OH2" with O next to Co). Show the overall charge 2+ outside square brackets. Do not label any bond angles or count any angles.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A molecule of butylbenzene, C6H5CH2CH2CH2CH3, can rotate about its single bonds. Count the six ring carbon atoms and every other atom that must always lie in the same plane as the ring carbon atoms. What is the total number of atoms?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw butylbenzene as a skeletal formula: a hexagon with a circle inside for the ring, and a zig-zag four-carbon chain on one ring carbon. Label the chain carbons 1 to 4, starting from the carbon bonded to the ring. Do not show any plane, shading or wedge bonds.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A benzene ring carries one -NH2 group and two chlorine atoms. Each chlorine atom is on a ring carbon that is separated from the carbon bonded to -NH2 by one other ring carbon, one on each side of the -NH2 group. What is the systematic name of this compound?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a benzene ring (hexagon with a circle) with NH2 on the top carbon, and Cl on the two ring carbons that are each one carbon away from the NH2 carbon (one on the left side, one on the right side of the ring). Do not number the ring carbons and do not write the name.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: 3-Nitrobenzoic acid is nitrated again, and one more -NO2 group is substituted into the ring. What is the main organic product?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw 3-nitrobenzoic acid: a benzene ring (hexagon with a circle) with COOH on the top carbon and NO2 on the ring carbon that is separated from it by one ring carbon, going clockwise. Do not number the ring carbons and do not mark any other position.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound W has a chlorine atom bonded directly to a benzene ring and a -CH2Cl group on the opposite ring carbon (the 1- and 4-positions): Cl-C6H4-CH2Cl. W is heated under reflux with an excess of aqueous sodium hydroxide. What is the main organic product?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a benzene ring (hexagon with a circle) with Cl bonded directly to the top ring carbon and a CH2Cl group on the bottom ring carbon (para to it). Label the compound W. Do not show any reagent or product.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Benzene-1,3-diol has OH groups on carbons 1 and 3 of a benzene ring, so carbons 2, 4, 5 and 6 each carry a hydrogen atom. An electrophile, E+, substitutes one of these hydrogen atoms. Each OH group directs in the same way as the OH group in phenol. How many different monosubstituted compounds are expected as the major products?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a benzene ring (hexagon with a circle). Number the ring carbons 1 to 6 going round the ring. Attach an OH group to carbon 1 and to carbon 3, and show an H atom on each of carbons 2, 4, 5 and 6. Do not mark any reacting position, arrow or product.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: 2-Naphthol, C10H7OH, reacts with the 4-methylbenzenediazonium ion, CH3C6H4N2+, in a coupling reaction. The product is an azo dye. What is the molecular formula of the azo dye?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw 2-naphthol as two fused hexagons with circles, with an OH group on carbon 2 and the ring carbons numbered. Beside it, separately, draw the 4-methylbenzenediazonium ion: a benzene ring with CH3 on one carbon and the group N≡N+ on the opposite carbon. Do not draw the product or any arrows.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound Z, HOC6H4CH(OH)COOH, has three OH groups: one bonded directly to the benzene ring, one in the CH(OH) group, and one in the COOH group. Which row gives the amount of NaOH that reacts with 1 mol of Z, and the amount of CO2 given off when 1 mol of Z reacts with excess aqueous sodium hydrogencarbonate?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a benzene ring (hexagon with circle). On one ring carbon draw an OH group. On the carbon opposite it draw a side chain CH(OH)–COOH, showing the C=O and O–H of the COOH group. Label the compound Z. No reagents or products.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound T, HOC6H4CH2CH2OH, has one OH group bonded directly to a benzene ring and one OH group at the end of a CH2CH2 chain. T is mixed with excess ethanoyl chloride, CH3COCl. What is the molecular formula of the organic product?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a benzene ring (hexagon with circle). On one ring carbon draw an OH group; on the carbon opposite it draw a CH2–CH2–OH chain. Label the compound T. Do not draw ethanoyl chloride or any product.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: The diazonium ion ClC6H4N2⁺ is made from 4-chlorophenylamine. It reacts with 4-methylphenol, CH3C6H4OH, in a coupling reaction to give a coloured azo compound. In 4-methylphenol, the OH group and the CH3 group are on opposite carbons of the ring (positions 1 and 4). Which row gives the solution in which the coupling is carried out and the ring carbon of 4-methylphenol that becomes bonded to the azo group?
options: in dilute hydrochloric acid; a ring carbon next to the CH3 group
in aqueous sodium hydroxide; a ring carbon next to the CH3 group
in aqueous sodium hydroxide; a ring carbon next to the OH group
in dilute hydrochloric acid; a ring carbon next to the OH group
jobs.authorBrief: Draw two separate structures side by side. Left: a benzene ring with a Cl atom at one position and an –N≡N⁺ group at the opposite (1,4) position, labelled "4-chlorobenzenediazonium ion". Right: a benzene ring with an OH group and a CH3 group at opposite (1,4) positions, labelled "4-methylphenol", with the ring carbons numbered 1 to 6 starting from the carbon that carries the OH group. Do not mark any ring carbon, and do not draw any product or any arrow joining the two structures.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A cyclic amide has a five-membered ring made of one N atom (with one H atom), one C=O carbon atom and three CH2 groups. The N atom is bonded directly to the C=O carbon atom. The amide is heated under reflux with an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid until hydrolysis is complete. Which organic species is present in the final solution, where the acid is still in excess?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw the displayed formula of pyrrolidin-2-one: a five-membered ring of one N atom (bearing one H), one carbon with a double-bonded O, and three CH2 groups. The N is bonded directly to the C=O carbon. Show all H atoms. Label the compound "cyclic amide". Do not show any reagent, arrow or product.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A mixture of three amino acids is placed in the centre of a gel soaked in a buffer at pH 6.0. A potential difference is applied across the gel, with a positive electrode at one end and a negative electrode at the other. Isoelectric points: glycine 6.0, lysine 9.7, glutamic acid 3.2. Which row describes how each amino acid moves?
options: glycine: does not move; lysine: towards the negative electrode; glutamic acid: towards the positive electrode
glycine: does not move; lysine: towards the positive electrode; glutamic acid: towards the negative electrode
glycine: towards the negative electrode; lysine: towards the negative electrode; glutamic acid: does not move
glycine: towards the positive electrode; lysine: does not move; glutamic acid: towards the positive electrode
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a horizontal rectangle of gel on a support, labelled "gel in buffer, pH 6.0". At the left end draw an electrode labelled "+" and at the right end an electrode labelled "−", both joined by wires to a d.c. power supply. Draw one small spot in the centre of the gel labelled "sample applied here". Do not show any separated spots or arrows.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A polyamide has the repeat unit –NH(CH2)4NHCO(CH2)8CO–. Which pair of monomers forms this polyamide?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw the repeat unit –NH–(CH2)4–NH–CO–(CH2)8–CO– in square brackets with an open bond at each end and a subscript n. Show each CH2 group explicitly (4 in the first chain, 8 in the second), the N–H bonds and the C=O groups. Do not name any monomer and do not show HCl or H2O.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
A section of a polymer chain is shown.

–OCH2CH2NHCOCH2CH2COOCH2CH2NHCOCH2CH2CO–

Which monomers were used to make this polymer?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw the displayed formula of the chain section –O–CH2–CH2–NH–CO–CH2–CH2–CO–O–CH2–CH2–NH–CO–CH2–CH2–CO– in one horizontal line, showing every C, H, N and O atom and every bond, with C=O drawn as a double bond to an O above or below the chain, and a short continuation bond at each end. Do not bracket a repeat unit, do not label any link and do not name any monomer.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
A drug molecule has the structural formula CH3CH(OH)CH(NH2)CH(CH3)COOH. Only one of its stereoisomers is active. A synthesis that is not stereoselective makes all the possible stereoisomers of this structure in equal amounts.

What percentage of the product is the active stereoisomer? Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Displayed formula of CH3CH(OH)CH(NH2)CH(CH3)COOH (3-amino-4-hydroxy-2-methylpentanoic acid) drawn flat, with every atom and bond shown: the five-carbon chain horizontal, the COOH group at the right end, the CH3 branch on C2, NH2 on C3 and OH on C4 drawn above or below the chain. Do not number the carbons, do not mark any carbon with an asterisk and do not use wedge or dashed bonds.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
The skeletal formula of compound K is a regular hexagon of lines. One side of the hexagon is a double line; the other five sides are single lines. No other atoms or groups are shown.

What is the molecular formula of K?
jobs.authorBrief: Skeletal formula only: a regular hexagon of lines with no atom symbols at the corners. One side is a double line (a second, slightly shorter line inside the ring); the other five sides are single lines. Label the figure "compound K". Do not write any C or H symbols, and do not draw a circle inside the ring.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem:
In compound M, five carbon atoms are joined by single bonds to form a ring. One ring carbon carries an OH group. A ring carbon next to it carries a CH3 group. No other groups are attached.

Which is the systematic name of M?
jobs.authorBrief: Skeletal formula: a regular pentagon of single lines. At one corner draw a line out of the ring ending in "OH". At a corner next to it draw a short line out of the ring (a methyl group, no symbol at its end). Label the figure "compound M". Do not number any carbon atom.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student plans this route to the compound (CH3)2CBrCHBrCH3, 2,3-dibromo-2-methylbutane. Step 1: 3-methylbutan-2-ol, CH3CH(OH)CH(CH3)2, is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid, and the alkene that forms is collected. Step 2: the alkene from step 1 is shaken with bromine dissolved in an organic solvent at room temperature. Which statement about the route is correct?
options: Step 1 is an elimination that gives only 2-methylbut-2-ene, because the OH group is on carbon 2 and the C=C bond must form between carbons 2 and 3.
Step 1 is a nucleophilic substitution in which HSO4⁻ replaces the OH group, and the alkene forms only in step 2.
Step 2 is an electrophilic addition in which a Br⁻ ion attacks the C=C bond first, and HBr forms as a by-product.
Step 1 is an elimination; 3-methylbut-1-ene also forms, and step 2 converts it into 1,2-dibromo-3-methylbutane, which must be separated from the product.
jobs.authorBrief: Three boxes left to right: 3-methylbutan-2-ol (CH3CH(OH)CH(CH3)2) → 2-methylbut-2-ene ((CH3)2C=CHCH3) → 2,3-dibromo-2-methylbutane ((CH3)2CBrCHBrCH3). Arrow 1 labelled "conc. H2SO4, heat". Arrow 2 labelled "Br2 in an organic solvent, room temperature". Do not show by-products, reaction types or mechanisms.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A mixture is separated by thin-layer chromatography. The baseline is 1.0 cm above the bottom edge of the plate. When the plate is removed, the solvent front is 9.0 cm above the bottom edge. The mixture gives two spots, with centres 2.6 cm and 6.2 cm above the bottom edge. Rf values for eight compounds, measured on the same type of plate with the same solvent: P 0.35, Q 0.65, R 0.18, S 0.69, T 0.20, U 0.80, V 0.58, W 0.29 (all to 2 decimal places). Which two compounds could be in the mixture?
jobs.authorBrief: A vertical rectangular TLC plate about 10 cm tall. Pencil baseline 1.0 cm above the bottom edge, labelled "baseline". Solvent front line 9.0 cm above the bottom edge, labelled "solvent front". Two spots on one vertical lane, centres 2.6 cm and 6.2 cm above the bottom edge. Dimension arrows from the bottom edge to the baseline, each spot centre and the solvent front, labelled 1.0 cm, 2.6 cm, 6.2 cm and 9.0 cm. No Rf values.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A mixture of three liquids, X, Y and Z, is dissolved in hexane and analysed by gas–liquid chromatography. The chromatogram has four peaks; the first is hexane. Each peak is close to a triangle, so its area can be taken as height × width at half height. The detector gives the same area for equal masses of X, Y and Z. Hexane: retention time 1.2 min, height 9.5 cm, width at half height 0.20 min. X: 3.1 min, 4.0 cm, 0.30 min. Y: 4.4 min, 6.0 cm, 0.25 min. Z: 6.8 min, 2.0 cm, 0.85 min. Calculate the percentage by mass of Z in the mixture of X, Y and Z, to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: detector response (y, no numbers) against retention time / min (x, 0 to 8). Four roughly triangular peaks: at 1.2 min labelled hexane (height 9.5 cm, width at half height 0.20 min); at 3.1 min labelled X (4.0 cm, 0.30 min); at 4.4 min labelled Y (6.0 cm, 0.25 min); at 6.8 min labelled Z (2.0 cm, 0.85 min). Mark the height and the width at half height on each peak. No areas or percentages.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: Compound H has three peaks in its proton NMR spectrum: δ 1.1 (doublet, relative area 6), δ 2.1 (singlet, relative area 3) and δ 2.6 (multiplet, relative area 1). Chemical shift data: alkyl C–H (R–CH3, R–CH2–R, R3CH) 0.9–2.0 ppm; H–C next to C=O (CH3CO–, –CH2CO–, –CHCO–) 2.0–2.7 ppm; H–C bonded to O (alcohols, ethers, esters) 3.3–5.1 ppm; H in –COOH 9.0–13.0 ppm. Which compound is H?
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis: chemical shift δ / ppm, from 4.0 on the left to 0 on the right; y-axis: absorption (no numbers). Peaks: a doublet centred at δ 1.1 labelled "6"; a singlet at δ 2.1 labelled "3"; a multiplet (seven small lines) centred at δ 2.6 labelled "1". A small TMS singlet at δ 0. No structural labels or group names.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student plans an investigation into the thermal stability of the Group 2 carbonates. The same amount in moles of magnesium, calcium, strontium and barium carbonate will be heated in turn in a hard-glass test tube with the same Bunsen flame. The gas given off passes into limewater, and the time taken for the limewater to turn cloudy is measured. Which hypothesis links the independent and dependent variables and agrees with the chemistry of Group 2?
options: The further down Group 2 the metal is, the longer the time for the limewater to turn cloudy, because the larger cation polarises the carbonate ion less.
The further down Group 2 the metal is, the shorter the time for the limewater to turn cloudy, because the larger cation polarises the carbonate ion more.
The further down Group 2 the metal is, the shorter the time for the limewater to turn cloudy, because the cation has a lower charge density.
The larger the volume of limewater used, the longer the time for the limewater to turn cloudy, because more carbon dioxide is needed.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view: a clamped hard-glass test tube containing a white solid labelled "Group 2 carbonate", heated from below by a Bunsen burner. A bung and bent delivery tube lead from the test tube into a second test tube labelled "limewater". Label the stopclock beside the apparatus. No values, no trend shown.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student plans to find the volume of hydrogen made when about 0.075 g of magnesium ribbon reacts with an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid at room temperature. The mass of magnesium must be recorded to three significant figures, and all the hydrogen must be collected and its volume measured in one go. (Ar: Mg, 24.3; molar gas volume at room conditions = 24.0 dm³ mol⁻¹) Which row shows apparatus suitable for both steps?
options: weighing: balance reading to 0.01 g; collecting: 100 cm³ gas syringe
weighing: balance reading to 0.0001 g; collecting: 50 cm³ gas syringe
weighing: balance reading to 0.0001 g; collecting: 100 cm³ gas syringe
weighing: balance reading to 0.01 g; collecting: 50 cm³ gas syringe
jobs.authorBrief: Side view: a conical flask with a bung, containing dilute hydrochloric acid, with a piece of magnesium ribbon held in a small open tube above the acid so it can be tipped in. A delivery tube from the bung leads to a horizontal gas syringe. Label: "dilute hydrochloric acid (excess)", "magnesium ribbon", "gas syringe". Do NOT show the capacity or scale of the syringe.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student measures the electrode potential, E, of a half-cell made of metal X dipping into solutions of X²⁺ ions of different concentration. The results fit the equation E = m lg[X²⁺] + c. Results (lg[X²⁺], then E / V): −3.0, −0.400; −2.5, −0.385; −2.0, −0.370; −1.5, −0.355; −1.0, −0.340 (end of table). The student plots E on the y-axis against lg[X²⁺] on the x-axis. The x-axis starts at lg[X²⁺] = −3.0, so the y-axis is drawn at this value. All five points lie on a straight line. What are the values of m and c?
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x-axis "lg[X²⁺]" from −3.0 to −1.0 (the y-axis is drawn at x = −3.0, as the stem says); y-axis "E / V" from −0.410 to −0.330. Plot the five points from the table: (−3.0, −0.400), (−2.5, −0.385), (−2.0, −0.370), (−1.5, −0.355), (−1.0, −0.340), with a straight line through them. Do not extend the line to lg[X²⁺] = 0 and do not mark any intercept or gradient value.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student finds the percentage purity of a sample of sodium carbonate. A weighed sample reacts with an excess of dilute hydrochloric acid in a flask. The carbon dioxide passes through a delivery tube into an upturned measuring cylinder filled with water, standing in a trough of water. The volume of gas is used to calculate the amount of sodium carbonate in the sample. Which statement identifies and explains a weakness of this procedure?
options: Carbon dioxide is fairly soluble in water, so the water level falls further than it should; the volume measured is too large and the purity calculated is too high.
The hydrochloric acid is in excess, so some acid is left over at the end; the purity calculated is too low.
The flask is not heated, so not all of the sodium carbonate reacts with the acid; the purity calculated is too low.
Carbon dioxide is fairly soluble in water, so some of it dissolves; the volume measured is too small and the purity calculated is too low.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view: a conical flask labelled "sodium carbonate + excess dilute hydrochloric acid", closed with a bung. A delivery tube runs from the bung into a trough of water and up into the mouth of an upturned measuring cylinder (labelled "measuring cylinder, full of water at the start") held by a clamp. Show bubbles leaving the end of the tube. No arrows or labels about gas dissolving.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student electroplates a copper key with silver, using a constant current. The mass of silver deposited is measured after different amounts of charge have passed. Results (charge / C, then mass of silver / g): 200, 0.22; 400, 0.45; 600, 0.67; 800, 0.89; 1000, 1.12 (end of table). When the student plots these points, all of them lie close to a straight line of best fit. Which statement about these data is correct?
options: The data are accurate, because a straight line shows that there is no systematic error.
The data are reliable, because none of the points is anomalous.
The data are unreliable, because the points do not all lie exactly on the line.
Points that do not lie exactly on the line should be removed before the gradient is found.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x-axis "charge / C" from 0 to 1000; y-axis "mass of silver / g" from 0 to 1.20. Plot the five points from the table: (200, 0.22), (400, 0.45), (600, 0.67), (800, 0.89), (1000, 1.12), and a straight line of best fit through the origin with the points scattered very slightly about it. No text on the graph about reliability or accuracy.

jobs.subject: chemistry
jobs.stem: A student adds 0.200 mol dm⁻³ sulfuric acid from a burette, 5.00 cm³ at a time, to 50.0 cm³ of aqueous barium hydroxide, and measures the electrical conductivity of the mixture after each addition. The conductivity falls to a minimum at the end-point and then rises. Results (volume of acid added / cm³, then conductivity / mS cm⁻¹): 0.00, 8.40; 5.00, 6.56; 10.00, 4.72; 15.00, 2.88; 20.00, 1.04; 25.00, 1.35; 30.00, 3.10; 35.00, 4.85; 40.00, 6.60 (end of table). Between which volumes of acid would extra readings be most useful for finding the end-point?
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: x-axis "volume of sulfuric acid added / cm³" from 0 to 40; y-axis "conductivity / mS cm⁻¹" from 0 to 9. Plot the nine points from the table only: (0, 8.40), (5, 6.56), (10, 4.72), (15, 2.88), (20, 1.04), (25, 1.35), (30, 3.10), (35, 4.85), (40, 6.60). Do not draw lines through the points and do not mark the end-point or any region.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A model car moves around a horizontal circular track of fixed radius. At one instant, the acceleration of the car has a magnitude of 2.0 m s⁻² and is directed at 60° to the velocity of the car, on the inside of the curve. Which statement describes the angular speed of the car at that instant?
options: It is constant, because the car stays on a circle of fixed radius.
It is decreasing, because only part of the acceleration is directed towards the centre.
It is constant, because the acceleration has a component towards the centre of the circle.
It is increasing, because the acceleration has a component in the direction of the velocity.
jobs.authorBrief: Plan view of a circle (the track) with its centre marked. Show the car as a small dot on the circle. From the dot draw a velocity arrow along the tangent, labelled "velocity". Draw a second arrow, labelled "acceleration, 2.0 m s⁻²", at 60° to the velocity arrow and pointing to the inside of the circle. Mark the angle between the arrows as 60°. Do not draw components of the acceleration.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A ball of mass 0.150 kg is tied to a light string. It moves in a vertical circle of radius 0.600 m. At the lowest point of the circle, the speed of the ball is 6.00 m s⁻¹. Air resistance is negligible and the acceleration of free fall g is 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the tension in the string when the ball is at the highest point of the circle. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view of a vertical circle with its centre marked. Draw the string as a line from the centre to a ball on the circle. Label the radius 0.600 m. Label the lowest point "lowest point, speed 6.00 m s⁻¹" and the highest point "highest point". Do not draw any force arrows.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A uniform lead sphere has a radius of 0.150 m. The density of lead is 1.13 × 10⁴ kg m⁻³. A small uniform sphere of mass 0.0800 kg and radius 0.0100 m rests touching the lead sphere. The volume of a sphere of radius r is (4/3)πr³ and the gravitational constant G is 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². Calculate the gravitational force between the two spheres. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a large circle (lead sphere) and a small circle (small sphere) touching at one point. Mark the centre of each. Label the large radius 0.150 m and the small radius 0.0100 m. Do not draw or label the distance between the two centres.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Three small spheres lie on a straight line on a smooth, horizontal surface. They can be treated as point masses. Sphere X has mass 3.0 kg and is at the 0 cm mark. Sphere Y has mass 1.0 kg and is at the 20 cm mark. Sphere Z has mass 2.0 kg and is at the 50 cm mark. The gravitational constant G is 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N m² kg⁻². Calculate the magnitude of the resultant gravitational force on sphere Y due to X and Z. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a horizontal scale from 0 to 50 cm. Place small spheres labelled X (3.0 kg) at 0 cm, Y (1.0 kg) at 20 cm and Z (2.0 kg) at 50 cm. Do not draw force arrows or the distances between the spheres.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Three metal blocks X, Y and Z are placed in a row on an insulating mat. X touches Y, and Y touches Z. X and Z do not touch. At the start, X is at 40.0 °C, Y is at 305 K and Z is at 310 K. Which row gives the direction of the net transfer of thermal energy at each contact at the start? Row A: X–Y contact from X to Y; Y–Z contact from Y to Z. Row B: X–Y contact from Y to X; Y–Z contact from Z to Y. Row C: X–Y contact from Y to X; Y–Z contact from Y to Z. Row D: X–Y contact from X to Y; Y–Z contact from Z to Y.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view of an insulating mat with three equal-sized rectangular metal blocks in a row, labelled X, Y and Z from left to right. X touches Y and Y touches Z; X and Z do not touch. Label each block with its starting temperature: "X: 40.0 °C", "Y: 305 K", "Z: 310 K". No arrows showing energy flow.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student heats a fixed mass of gas at constant volume and measures its pressure p at three temperatures θ: p = 104.0 kPa at θ = 20.0 °C, p = 114.8 kPa at θ = 50.0 °C and p = 125.6 kPa at θ = 80.0 °C. The pressure varies linearly with temperature. The student extrapolates the line to the temperature at which the pressure would be zero. Use only these data. Calculate the value of absolute zero that this experiment gives. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: horizontal θ / °C from −300 to 100, vertical p / kPa from 0 to 140. Plot the three points (20.0, 104.0), (50.0, 114.8), (80.0, 125.6) with crosses and draw a solid straight line through them. Extend the line to the left as a dashed line towards the θ axis. Do not mark or label where the line meets the θ axis.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A heater of constant power is put into 0.200 kg of a solid at 20.0 °C. All the energy from the heater goes into the sample. The table shows the temperature of the sample at three times. At t = 0 s it is at 20.0 °C, at t = 120 s it is at 80.0 °C and at t = 420 s it is at 80.0 °C. The sample is solid until t = 120 s. Between t = 120 s and t = 420 s the temperature stays at 80.0 °C, and at t = 420 s the sample has just finished melting. The specific heat capacity of the solid is 1.50 kJ kg⁻¹ K⁻¹. Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion of the substance.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: horizontal time / s from 0 to 450, vertical temperature / °C from 0 to 100. Straight line from (0, 20.0) to (120, 80.0), then a horizontal line from (120, 80.0) to (420, 80.0). Mark the points at t = 0, 120 and 420 s. No labels for the stages and no values of energy or power.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A small bubble of air is released at the bottom of a lake, 12.0 m below the surface. The water at the bottom is at 8.0 °C and the water at the surface is at 24.0 °C. The air in the bubble behaves as an ideal gas, and its temperature is always the same as the water around it. Atmospheric pressure is 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa. The density of the water is 1000 kg m⁻³ and g = 9.81 m s⁻². The pressure difference due to a depth Δh of liquid is Δp = ρgΔh. Calculate the ratio (volume of the bubble just below the surface) / (volume of the bubble at the bottom). Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Vertical cross-section of a lake. Mark the water surface and the lake bed, with a vertical arrow between them labelled "12.0 m". Draw a small circle (bubble) at the bottom labelled "8.0 °C" for the water there, and a second circle just below the surface labelled "24.0 °C" for the water there. Label the air above "atmospheric pressure 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa". Draw both bubbles the same size so the drawing does not show the volume change.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: In a simple model, one gas molecule of mass 4.65 × 10⁻²⁶ kg moves backwards and forwards along a straight line between two parallel walls that are 0.200 m apart. It travels at 480 m s⁻¹ at right angles to the walls and rebounds from each wall with the same speed. It does not hit any other molecule. Calculate the average force that the molecule exerts on one of the walls, to three significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Two parallel vertical walls drawn 0.200 m apart (dimension arrow labelled 0.200 m). A small filled circle between them labelled "molecule, mass 4.65 × 10⁻²⁶ kg" with a horizontal arrow at right angles to the walls labelled "480 m s⁻¹". No force arrows, no values other than these.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A machine moves a horizontal tray up and down with simple harmonic motion at a frequency of 4.00 Hz. A small block rests on the tray. For simple harmonic motion, a = −ω²x. The acceleration of free fall g is 9.81 m s⁻². Calculate the largest amplitude for which the block stays in contact with the tray all the time, to three significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view of a horizontal tray on a vertical rod attached to a box labelled "shaking machine". A small rectangular block rests on top of the tray. A double-headed vertical arrow beside the tray labelled "vertical oscillation, frequency 4.00 Hz". No amplitude value and no acceleration arrows.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: An object moves with simple harmonic motion of period T. The graph of its displacement x against time t is a cosine curve: when t = 0, x = +x₀ (the positive maximum); when t = T/4, x = 0; when t = T/2, x = −x₀. Which statement describes the graph of its velocity against time during the first quarter of the cycle, from t = 0 to t = T/4?
options: It starts at its maximum positive value and decreases to zero.
It starts at zero and increases to its maximum positive value.
It starts at its maximum negative value and increases to zero.
It starts at zero and decreases to its maximum negative value.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: displacement x (vertical, with +x₀ and −x₀ marked) against time t (horizontal, with T/4, T/2, 3T/4 and T marked). One full cycle of a cosine curve: x = +x₀ at t = 0, zero at T/4, −x₀ at T/2, zero at 3T/4, +x₀ at T. No velocity or acceleration curves.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: An object moves with simple harmonic motion. The table shows how its acceleration a varies with time t over one complete cycle; a smooth curve through these values has the shape of a sine curve. (t / s: 0, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.60, 0.70, 0.80; a / m s⁻²: 0, −1.70, −2.40, −1.70, 0, +1.70, +2.40, +1.70, 0, in the same order) For simple harmonic motion, a = −ω²x and v = ±ω√(x₀² − x²). Calculate the maximum speed of the object, to three significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: acceleration a / m s⁻² (vertical, −3.0 to +3.0) against time t / s (horizontal, 0 to 0.80). Plot the nine points from the table (0, 0), (0.10, −1.70), (0.20, −2.40), (0.30, −1.70), (0.40, 0), (0.50, +1.70), (0.60, +2.40), (0.70, +1.70), (0.80, 0) joined by a smooth curve. No velocity or displacement curves.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A damped oscillator is displaced and released. Its displacement–time graph gives the maximum displacement on the same side of the equilibrium position after each period T. Time 0: 50.0 mm. Time T: 40.0 mm. Time 2T: 32.0 mm. The pattern continues and the period stays the same. Calculate the percentage of the energy of the oscillation at time 0 that is still in the oscillation at time 4T. The options are given to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: displacement / mm (vertical, from −60 to +60) against time (horizontal, marked 0, T, 2T). Draw a smooth oscillation starting at a maximum of +50.0 mm at time 0, with positive maxima of 40.0 mm at T and 32.0 mm at 2T, and the matching smaller negative minima between them.
