Label the three positive maxima with their values. Stop the curve just after 2T; do not draw or label anything at 3T or 4T.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Two large parallel plates X and Y are 12.0 cm apart in a vacuum. Plate X is at a potential of +250 V and plate Y is at a potential of −350 V. Point P is between the plates, 4.0 cm from plate Y. Edge effects are negligible. Calculate the electric potential at P.
jobs.authorBrief: Two long horizontal parallel plates, X on top and Y below, 12.0 cm apart (dimension arrow). Label X "+250 V" and Y "−350 V". Mark a dot P between the plates with a dimension arrow of 4.0 cm from P down to plate Y. No field lines, no other values.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: An alpha particle enters the space between two horizontal parallel plates, midway between them. It moves parallel to the plates with a speed of 2.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹. The plates are 5.0 cm long and 1.6 cm apart, and the potential difference between them is 2.0 kV. Edge effects and the weight of the alpha particle are negligible. The elementary charge e is 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and the mass of an alpha particle is 6.64 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. For uniform acceleration from initial velocity u, s = ut + ½at². Calculate the vertical distance through which the alpha particle has been deflected when it leaves the field. The options are given to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Two horizontal parallel plates, 5.0 cm long (dimension arrow along the plates) and 1.6 cm apart (dimension arrow between them). A short arrow labelled "alpha particle, 2.0 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹" approaches from the left, midway between the plates. Label the p.d. between the plates as 2.0 kV, without marking which plate is positive. Do not draw the path of the alpha particle inside the plates.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: The electric potential V varies with distance x along a straight line. A graph of V against x is a curve. The tangent to the curve at x = 4.0 cm passes through the points (x = 0, V = 360 V) and (x = 10.0 cm, V = 0). At x = 4.0 cm the potential is 216 V. Which row gives the magnitude and direction of the electric field strength at x = 4.0 cm?
options: magnitude: 3.6 × 10³ V m⁻¹ · direction: towards decreasing x
magnitude: 3.6 × 10³ V m⁻¹ · direction: towards increasing x
magnitude: 5.4 × 10³ V m⁻¹ · direction: towards increasing x
magnitude: 9.0 × 10³ V m⁻¹ · direction: towards increasing x
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: V / V (vertical, 0 to 400) against x / cm (horizontal, 0 to 10). Draw a smooth curve that falls as x increases and passes through (4.0, 216). Draw a straight tangent touching the curve at x = 4.0 cm, running from (0, 360) to (10.0, 0), and label these two end points and the point of contact. Do not write a gradient value or any field value.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Two point charges of +7.0 nC and −3.0 nC are fixed in a vacuum. Point P is 0.30 m from the +7.0 nC charge and 0.40 m from the −3.0 nC charge. The lines from P to the two charges are at 90° to each other. The electric potential V at a distance r from a point charge Q is given by V = Q / (4πε₀r). The permittivity of free space ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F m⁻¹. Calculate the electric potential at P. The options are given to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: A right-angled triangle with the right angle at P. One other corner holds a dot labelled "+7.0 nC", 0.30 m from P; the third corner holds a dot labelled "−3.0 nC", 0.40 m from P. Label the two sides from P with their lengths and mark the right angle at P. No arrows, no field lines.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Capacitor P (3.0 μF) and capacitor Q (6.0 μF) are connected in series. Capacitor R (5.0 μF) is connected in parallel with the pair P and Q. The combination is connected to a 12 V supply with negligible internal resistance. All three capacitors were uncharged at the start. Calculate the total charge that flows from the supply to charge the capacitors.
jobs.authorBrief: Circuit diagram: d.c. supply labelled 12 V. One branch contains capacitor P (3.0 μF) and capacitor Q (6.0 μF) one after the other; a second branch contains capacitor R (5.0 μF) alone; both branches connect to the two supply terminals. Label each capacitor with its letter and value. Show no charges or p.d.s.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A capacitor with a ceramic insulator does not have a constant capacitance. While it is charged, the potential difference V across it changes with the charge Q on it as shown in the table. In the table, the values of Q / μC are 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40, and the matching values of V / V are 0, 2.0, 4.5, 7.5 and 11.0 in the same order. Assume the graph of V against Q is a straight line between neighbouring points. Calculate the energy stored when the charge is 40 μC.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: Q / μC horizontal from 0 to 40, V / V vertical from 0 to 12. Plot the points (0, 0), (10, 2.0), (20, 4.5), (30, 7.5), (40, 11.0) and join neighbouring points with straight line segments. Grid lines every 5 μC and every 1 V. No shading.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A horizontal metal rod of length 0.40 m and mass 12 g rests on two supports. The rod points east–west. A uniform horizontal magnetic field of flux density 0.050 T points due north across the whole rod. The current in the rod is adjusted until the magnetic force on the rod is just equal to its weight and the rod is about to lift. The acceleration of free fall g is 9.81 m s⁻². Which row gives the direction and the size of the current in the rod? The current is given to two significant figures.
options: direction: from west to east · current: 0.60 A
direction: from east to west · current: 0.60 A
direction: from west to east · current: 5.9 A
direction: from east to west · current: 5.9 A
jobs.authorBrief: Perspective sketch: a horizontal metal rod (length 0.40 m, mass 12 g) lying east–west across two supports, joined by leads to a variable d.c. supply. A compass rose shows N, E, S, W and Up. Arrows labelled B = 0.050 T point north across the rod. Do not show the current direction or the force.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A Hall probe contains a rectangular slice of semiconductor. The current is along the length of the slice. The Hall voltage is measured between the two long edges of the slice, which are 6.0 mm apart. The thickness of the slice is 0.50 mm. A uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.25 T acts at right angles to the current and to the line joining the two edges. The Hall voltage is steady at 3.0 mV. Calculate the drift speed of the charge carriers in the slice.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a thin rectangular slice in 3-D. Label the width between the two long edges "6.0 mm" and the thickness "0.50 mm". Arrow along the length labelled "current". Arrow labelled "B = 0.25 T" at right angles to the current and to the 6.0 mm width (through the thickness). Voltmeter connected between the two long edges, labelled "3.0 mV". No carriers or charges drawn.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Three long straight parallel wires X, Y and Z are vertical and fixed in one plane. Y is midway between X and Z, and the separation of neighbouring wires is d. The currents are: X, current I upwards; Y, current I upwards; Z, current 2I downwards. The force per unit length between two long parallel wires is proportional to the product of their currents and inversely proportional to their separation. Which row describes the resultant magnetic force on wire X and on wire Y?
options: force on X: zero · force on Y: towards X
force on X: away from Y · force on Y: towards X
force on X: zero · force on Y: towards Z
force on X: towards Y · force on Y: towards X
jobs.authorBrief: Draw three long vertical parallel lines labelled X, Y, Z from left to right. Mark the separation between X and Y as d and between Y and Z as d. On X an upward arrow labelled I, on Y an upward arrow labelled I, on Z a downward arrow labelled 2I. Do not draw any force arrows.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: At a place on the Earth's surface, the Earth's magnetic field has a flux density of 52.0 μT. The field is directed at 65.0° below the horizontal. A square loop of wire of side 1.50 m lies flat on horizontal ground. Calculate the magnetic flux through the loop.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view and small perspective sketch: a square loop flat on a horizontal ground line, side labelled 1.50 m. A straight arrow labelled "B = 52.0 μT" pointing downwards into the ground at an angle; mark the angle between the arrow and the horizontal as 65.0°. Do not draw components of B.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A flat rectangular coil of 80 turns measures 5.0 cm by 4.0 cm. It moves at a steady speed into a region of uniform magnetic field of flux density 0.25 T. The field is perpendicular to the plane of the coil and is zero outside the region. At one instant, 3.0 cm of the 5.0 cm length of the coil is inside the region. Calculate the magnetic flux linkage of the coil at this instant.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a shaded rectangular region filled with crosses (field into the page) labelled "B = 0.25 T". A rectangular coil, 5.0 cm long and 4.0 cm wide, labelled "80 turns", moves to the right into the region; its leading 4.0 cm side is inside. Label the part of the length inside the region "3.0 cm". Arrow showing the direction of motion.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: An alternating voltage is shown on an oscilloscope. The time from a positive peak of the trace to the next negative peak is 4.0 ms. Calculate the frequency of the alternating voltage.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw about two cycles of a sine-shaped trace of voltage against time. Mark one positive peak and the next negative peak with dotted vertical lines and a double-headed arrow between them labelled "4.0 ms". No other time values or grid scale on the time axis.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A sinusoidal alternating supply is rectified. The diodes are ideal and there is no smoothing capacitor. The table gives the output p.d. V across the load resistor at different times t. The pattern then repeats. Table: t / ms and V / V: 0 ms, 0 V; 2.5 ms, 4.24 V; 5.0 ms, 6.00 V; 7.5 ms, 4.24 V; 10.0 ms, 0 V; 12.5 ms, 4.24 V; 15.0 ms, 6.00 V; 17.5 ms, 4.24 V; 20.0 ms, 0 V. Which row gives the type of rectification and the frequency of the supply?
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: V / V from 0 to 8 (vertical) and t / ms from 0 to 20 (horizontal). Plot the nine points from the table: (0, 0), (2.5, 4.24), (5.0, 6.00), (7.5, 4.24), (10.0, 0), (12.5, 4.24), (15.0, 6.00), (17.5, 4.24), (20.0, 0), joined by a smooth sinusoidal-shaped curve through the points. No labels naming the type of rectification or the supply frequency.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A sinusoidal alternating supply of r.m.s. p.d. 6.0 V and negligible internal resistance is connected to an ideal diode in series with a resistor of resistance 2.0 kΩ. Calculate the largest p.d. across the diode at any time during one cycle of the supply. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a sinusoidal a.c. supply symbol labelled "6.0 V r.m.s.", a diode symbol and a resistor labelled "2.0 kΩ" connected in a single series loop. Mark the p.d. across the diode with a voltmeter symbol connected across it. Do not show any values of the p.d. across the diode.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A bridge rectifier of four ideal diodes is connected to a 50 Hz sinusoidal supply and a load resistor. There is no smoothing capacitor. One of the diodes breaks and becomes an open circuit. The other three diodes still work normally. Which row describes the output now?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a standard bridge rectifier (four diodes in a diamond) with the a.c. supply across one diagonal and the load resistor across the other diagonal. Mark one diode with a cross and the label "open circuit". Label the supply "50 Hz". Do not draw any output waveform.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A sinusoidal supply of r.m.s. p.d. 12.0 V and frequency 50 Hz is connected to a single ideal diode in series with a load resistor of resistance 1.2 kΩ. A capacitor of capacitance 470 μF is connected in parallel with the load resistor. Assume that the capacitor is charged to the peak p.d. at each peak of the output, and then discharges through the load resistor only, for the whole time until the next peak of the output. During the discharge the p.d. V across the capacitor is given by V = V₀e^(−t/RC). Calculate the peak-to-peak ripple of the output p.d. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a sinusoidal a.c. supply labelled "12.0 V r.m.s., 50 Hz" in series with one diode. Across the output connect a capacitor labelled "470 μF" in parallel with a resistor labelled "1.2 kΩ". Do not draw any output waveform or ripple values.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: In an electron diffraction tube, electrons are accelerated from rest and then pass through a thin layer of graphite. They form rings on a screen. The accelerating potential difference is increased from 2.5 kV to 10 kV. The diffraction angles stay small, and relativistic effects can be ignored. How does the radius of one particular ring change?
options: It increases to four times its original value.
It increases to twice its original value.
It decreases to half its original value.
It decreases to one quarter of its original value.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a horizontal evacuated glass tube. Left: an electron gun (heated cathode and an anode with a small hole) connected to a supply labelled "accelerating p.d. V". Middle: a thin graphite film across the beam, labelled "graphite". Right end: a screen, drawn face-on beside the tube, showing two concentric rings around a central spot. Mark the radius of the inner ring with an arrow labelled r. Do not give any values or show the pattern at a second p.d.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A low-pressure gas in a discharge tube glows when there is a current in it. The light from the tube is viewed through a diffraction grating. Which row describes the spectrum that is seen and how it is formed? Row A: a continuous band of all colours; electrons in the atoms move to lower energy levels and emit photons. Row B: bright lines of certain colours on a dark background; electrons in the atoms move to higher energy levels and emit photons. Row C: bright lines of certain colours on a dark background; electrons in the atoms move to lower energy levels and emit photons. Row D: dark lines across a continuous band of colours; electrons in the atoms move to lower energy levels and emit photons.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a sealed glass discharge tube containing low-pressure gas, with an electrode at each end connected to a high-voltage supply. In front of the tube, draw a diffraction grating and, beyond it, an eye. Label "low-pressure gas", "high-voltage supply" and "diffraction grating". Do not draw, colour or describe any spectrum.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student measures the count rate C from a sample of a single radioactive nuclide at different times t. The count rate is corrected for background. The results, as pairs (t / min, ln (C / min⁻¹)), are (0, 6.80), (10, 6.34), (20, 5.88), (30, 5.41) and (40, 4.95). The count rate is given by C = C₀e^(−λt), and λ = 0.693 / t½. Find the half-life of the nuclide, to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: t / min from 0 to 40 (horizontal) and ln (C / min⁻¹) from 4.5 to 7.0 (vertical). Plot the five points from the table: (0, 6.80), (10, 6.34), (20, 5.88), (30, 5.41), (40, 4.95). Draw one best-fit straight line through them. Do not mark a gradient triangle, a half-life or any calculated value.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: An ultrasound probe on the skin sends a pulse into the body, at right angles to the surfaces of an organ. The pulse passes through soft tissue, in which the speed of ultrasound is 1540 m s⁻¹, and then through the organ, in which the speed of ultrasound is 1600 m s⁻¹. The echo from the front surface of the organ reaches the probe 54.0 μs after the pulse is sent. The echo from the back surface of the organ reaches the probe 81.0 μs after the pulse is sent. Calculate the thickness of the organ.
jobs.authorBrief: Horizontal axis: time / μs from 0 to 100. Vertical axis: signal (no scale). Draw a large spike at t = 0 labelled "emitted pulse", an echo peak at 54.0 μs labelled "front surface of organ" and a smaller echo peak at 81.0 μs labelled "back surface of organ". Do not mark the time difference or any distance.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: An ultrasound probe sends a pulse at right angles into a test block made of three layers of material, A, B and C, in that order. The specific acoustic impedances of A, B and C are in the ratio 1.0 : 2.0 : 8.0, in that order. The intensity reflection coefficient of a boundary is IR / I₀ = (Z₁ − Z₂)² / (Z₁ + Z₂)². Ignore attenuation in the layers and any loss at the probe. Calculate the intensity of the echo from the B–C boundary that reaches the probe, as a fraction of the intensity of the pulse sent into layer A.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a probe touching the left face of a test block made of three parallel flat layers in contact, labelled A (next to the probe), B (middle) and C (right). Show a horizontal arrow from the probe through A and B to the B–C boundary, and a returning arrow back to the probe. Label the A–B boundary and the B–C boundary. Give no impedance values or intensities on the figure.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Two narrow parallel X-ray beams, P and Q, of equal intensity pass through a limb that is 8.0 cm thick. Beam P passes through soft tissue only. Beam Q passes through soft tissue and through a layer of bone of thickness x, so that its total path in the limb is also 8.0 cm. The linear attenuation coefficient is 0.18 cm⁻¹ for soft tissue and 1.20 cm⁻¹ for bone. Where the beams leave the limb, the ratio (intensity of beam Q) / (intensity of beam P) is 0.10 exactly. Calculate x. The options are given to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw two horizontal parallel arrows labelled P and Q passing through a rectangle of soft tissue 8.0 cm wide. On path Q only, show a bone layer inside the rectangle with its thickness labelled x. Put a detector strip on the right. Label the 8.0 cm width and the symbol x only; give no intensities and no value for x.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A PET scanner has a circular ring of detectors with a diameter of 0.84 m. The scanner treats two gamma-ray photons as coming from the same annihilation event only if they are detected within a time interval Δt of each other. An annihilation event can happen anywhere inside the ring. Speed of light c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. What is the smallest value of Δt for which every annihilation event inside the ring can be accepted?
jobs.authorBrief: End-on view of a PET scanner: a circle made of small rectangular detector blocks, with a simple outline of a patient cross-section in the centre. Mark the diameter of the ring with a double-headed arrow labelled 0.84 m. Do not draw any photon paths or annihilation points.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A star in our galaxy moves in a circular orbit around a companion star. The plane of the orbit contains the line from the Earth to the star. The whole star system also moves away from the Earth at a constant velocity. A hydrogen line with a laboratory wavelength of 656.28 nm is observed in the light from the star. Over one orbit, the observed wavelength of this line varies smoothly between a minimum of 656.10 nm and a maximum of 656.90 nm. Use Δλ/λ ≈ v/c, where c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹. Calculate the orbital speed of the star. The options are given to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: time (no values needed) horizontally; observed wavelength / nm vertically from 656.00 to 657.00. Draw one full cycle of a smooth sinusoidal curve with minimum 656.10 and maximum 656.90, both labelled on the axis. Draw a horizontal dashed line at 656.28 labelled "laboratory wavelength". Do not mark the middle value of the curve.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: Three galaxies, A, M and B, lie on a straight line, with M between A and B. The distance from A to M is 2.0 units and the distance from M to B is 3.0 units. Over a certain time, the Universe expands so that every distance between galaxies doubles. Which statement describes the motion of M and B, as measured by an observer in galaxy A?
options: M and B both move towards A, because only an observer at the centre of the Universe sees galaxies moving away.
M and B both move away from A at the same speed.
M and B both move away from A, and M moves away 2.5 times as fast as B.
M and B both move away from A, and B moves away 2.5 times as fast as M.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw three small galaxy symbols on a horizontal straight line, labelled A (left), M (middle) and B (right). Mark the gap A to M with a double-headed arrow labelled 2.0 units and the gap M to B with a double-headed arrow labelled 3.0 units. Do not draw any velocity arrows.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student finds the RQ of blowfly larvae using three respirometers in a water-bath at 30 °C. The capillary tubes all have the same diameter. Tube 1 contains larvae and potassium hydroxide solution, which absorbs carbon dioxide. Tube 2 contains the same mass of larvae and water instead of potassium hydroxide solution. Tube 3 contains glass beads with the same volume as the larvae, and water; it shows any changes caused by the surroundings. After 20 minutes, the coloured liquid in each capillary tube has moved towards the tube by these distances: Tube 1, 50 mm; Tube 2, 9 mm; Tube 3, 3 mm. Work out the RQ of the larvae. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a water-bath labelled 30 °C holding three boiling tubes labelled Tube 1, Tube 2 and Tube 3. Tube 1: blowfly larvae on a wire-gauze platform above potassium hydroxide solution. Tube 2: blowfly larvae on a wire-gauze platform above water. Tube 3: glass beads on a wire-gauze platform above water. Each tube is sealed by a bung with a screw clip and joined to a capillary tube with a millimetre scale and a drop of coloured liquid. Show no distances and no arrows.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: Brown fat cells in newborn mammals have many mitochondria. The inner mitochondrial membrane of these cells contains a channel protein that lets protons diffuse back into the matrix without passing through ATP synthase. Which statement describes respiration in these mitochondria, compared with mitochondria that do not have this channel protein?
options: Electron transport continues, but less ATP is made for each molecule of oxygen used, and more energy is released as heat.
Electron transport stops, because protons can no longer be moved across the inner membrane.
Electron transport continues and more ATP is made, because protons return to the matrix faster.
Electron transport stops, because reduced NAD can no longer be formed in the Krebs cycle.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a horizontal section of inner mitochondrial membrane (phospholipid bilayer) with the intermembrane space above and the matrix below, both labelled. In the membrane draw a row of electron carrier proteins labelled "electron transport chain", an ATP synthase labelled "ATP synthase", and a separate protein labelled "channel protein". Draw one arrow labelled H+ passing down through the channel protein from the intermembrane space into the matrix. Do not show ATP, heat or arrows through ATP synthase.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A mitochondrion has an outer membrane, an inner membrane folded into cristae, an intermembrane space and a matrix. Which part is matched with its correct function?
options: cristae: contain the enzymes of the Krebs cycle
intermembrane space: contains the enzymes of the link reaction
matrix: contains the enzymes of the Krebs cycle
outer membrane: holds the carriers of the electron transport chain
jobs.authorBrief: Longitudinal section of one mitochondrion (about 2 μm long): smooth outer membrane; inner membrane folded into several cristae; narrow intermembrane space between the membranes; matrix shown with a small loop of DNA and ribosomes drawn as dots. Label lines to: outer membrane, inner membrane, crista, intermembrane space, matrix. Write no functions on the figure.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: Two varieties of rice, P and Q, grow in a field that floods slowly. The table shows the water depth and the height of the tallest leaf tip of each variety above the soil. Day 0: water 10 cm, P 40 cm, Q 40 cm. Day 4: water 30 cm, P 52 cm, Q 44 cm. Day 8: water 50 cm, P 66 cm, Q 47 cm. Day 12: water 70 cm, P 82 cm, Q 49 cm. On day 20, 85% of plants of variety P and 15% of plants of variety Q are still alive. Which explanation of the difference in survival is consistent with the data?
options: Variety Q survives less well because all of its leaves were below the water surface from day 4 onwards.
Variety Q survives less well because its stems stopped growing completely once they were below the water surface.
Variety P survives better because its stems grow fast enough to keep its upper leaves above the water, so the leaves can still exchange gases with the air.
Variety P survives better because its roots carry out ethanol fermentation, which transfers more energy to ATP than aerobic respiration.
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis: time / days, 0 to 12. y-axis: height or depth / cm, 0 to 90. Three lines with plotted points at days 0, 4, 8 and 12: water depth (10, 30, 50, 70); variety P (40, 52, 66, 82); variety Q (40, 44, 47, 49). Key naming the three lines. No labels about survival or submergence.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A respirometer contains 5.0 g of germinating mung beans and soda lime, in a water-bath at 30 °C. A control respirometer contains glass beads of the same volume. In 15 minutes, the liquid in the capillary tube of the bean respirometer moves 36 mm towards the beans, and the liquid in the control moves 4 mm towards the glass beads. The capillary tube has an internal diameter of 0.80 mm. The volume of a cylinder is πr²h. Calculate the rate of oxygen uptake by the beans. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Water-bath labelled 30 °C holding two boiling tubes. Each tube: soda lime at the bottom, a wire-gauze platform, then germinating mung beans (test tube, label "5.0 g germinating mung beans") or glass beads (control). Each tube has a bung with a capillary tube bent horizontally along a mm scale, containing a short index of coloured liquid, and a side tube with a tap or screw clip. Label: soda lime, wire gauze, capillary tube (internal diameter 0.80 mm), coloured liquid, scale / mm. Do not show the distances moved.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: The table shows the absorption spectrum of a pigment extract from the leaves of a plant and the action spectrum for photosynthesis of the same leaves. 400 nm: absorbance 0.70, rate 40%; 450 nm: 1.00, 75%; 500 nm: 0.40, 45%; 550 nm: 0.10, 15%; 600 nm: 0.20, 35%; 650 nm: 0.60, 90%; 700 nm: 0.15, 10%. Which statement is correct?
options: The wavelength at which the extract absorbs most light is also the wavelength that gives the highest rate of photosynthesis.
For each unit of absorbance, the rate of photosynthesis at 650 nm is twice the rate at 450 nm.
Light of 550 nm is not absorbed by the pigments, so it is not used in photosynthesis.
The rate of photosynthesis at 600 nm is lower than at 700 nm because the extract absorbs less light at 600 nm.
jobs.authorBrief: Shared x-axis: wavelength / nm, 400 to 700. Left y-axis: absorbance, 0 to 1.0. Right y-axis: relative rate of photosynthesis / %, 0 to 100. Plot points at 400, 450, 500, 550, 600, 650 and 700 nm. Absorbance: 0.70, 1.00, 0.40, 0.10, 0.20, 0.60, 0.15. Rate: 40, 75, 45, 15, 35, 90, 10. Join each set with a smooth line; key naming the absorption spectrum and the action spectrum. No other annotation.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student separates leaf pigments by paper chromatography. She measures all distances from the bottom edge of the paper. The pencil origin line is 1.5 cm from the bottom edge. The centre of one spot is 6.6 cm from the bottom edge, and the solvent front is 9.8 cm from the bottom edge. The Rf values in this solvent are 0.95 for carotene, 0.71 for xanthophyll, 0.61 for chlorophyll a and 0.45 for chlorophyll b. What is the Rf value of the spot, and which pigment is it?
jobs.authorBrief: Vertical strip of chromatography paper. Pencil origin line 1.5 cm above the bottom edge; solvent front line 9.8 cm above the bottom edge; one spot centred 6.6 cm above the bottom edge, labelled "spot"; two or three faint unlabelled spots elsewhere. A cm scale along the side starting at 0 at the bottom edge. Labels: origin line, solvent front. No pigment names or Rf values.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A leaf in a chamber at 20 °C is exposed to different light intensities at two carbon dioxide concentrations. Light intensities used (arbitrary units): 10, 20, 40, 60, 80, in that order. Rate of carbon dioxide uptake (arbitrary units) at 0.04% carbon dioxide: 4.1, 8.0, 11.5, 11.6, 11.6, respectively. At 0.12% carbon dioxide: 4.1, 8.1, 15.8, 21.9, 22.0, respectively. Which conclusion is supported by the data?
options: At a light intensity of 20 units, carbon dioxide concentration limits the rate at 0.04% carbon dioxide.
At a light intensity of 60 units, light intensity limits the rate at 0.12% carbon dioxide.
At a light intensity of 60 units, carbon dioxide concentration limits the rate at 0.04% carbon dioxide.
At a light intensity of 80 units, temperature limits the rate at 0.04% carbon dioxide.
jobs.authorBrief: Plot the table values. x-axis: light intensity / arbitrary units, 0 to 80. y-axis: rate of carbon dioxide uptake / arbitrary units, 0 to 25. Two lines with crosses at each point, labelled "0.04% carbon dioxide" (4.1, 8.0, 11.5, 11.6, 11.6) and "0.12% carbon dioxide" (4.1, 8.1, 15.8, 21.9, 22.0) at light intensities 10, 20, 40, 60, 80. No labels for limiting factors.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student uses an aquatic plant, Cabomba, in a tube of water to investigate the effect of carbon dioxide concentration on the rate of photosynthesis. She changes the carbon dioxide concentration by adding different masses of sodium hydrogencarbonate to the water. She counts the bubbles of gas released from the cut stem in 5 minutes. A lamp is placed 15 cm from the tube. Which row gives a variable that must be standardised and a suitable method of standardising it?
options: a control: set up a tube that contains no plant
temperature: stand the tube in a thermostatically controlled water-bath
carbon dioxide concentration: add the same mass of sodium hydrogencarbonate to each tube
number of bubbles: count the bubbles for 5 minutes at each concentration
jobs.authorBrief: Side view: a boiling tube held in a clamp, filled with water, with a sprig of an aquatic plant held upside down so the cut end of the stem points up; small bubbles rise from the cut end. A bench lamp beside the tube with a ruler showing 15 cm between lamp and plant. Label: "sodium hydrogencarbonate solution". Draw no water-bath, thermometer or control tube.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A diagram of a kidney cut lengthways shows four labels. P is a thin, tough layer that covers the outside of the kidney. Q is a granular band of tissue just inside P. R is one of several cone-shaped pyramids with fine stripes, inside Q. S is a funnel-shaped space at the centre of the kidney into which the pyramids open. Which row names P, Q, R and S?
options: P Bowman’s capsule; Q cortex; R medulla; S renal pelvis
P fibrous capsule; Q medulla; R cortex; S renal pelvis
P fibrous capsule; Q cortex; R medulla; S renal pelvis
P fibrous capsule; Q cortex; R medulla; S ureter
jobs.authorBrief: Longitudinal section of a human kidney. Label lines only, letters P to S: P on the thin outer covering; Q on the granular outer band of tissue just inside P; R on one of the striped cone-shaped pyramids; S on the funnel-shaped space at the centre into which the pyramids open. Show the vessels and the tube at the hilum unlabelled. No region names on the drawing.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A photomicrograph shows a transverse section through the medulla of a kidney. It shows many cut tubes of two kinds: wide tubes lined by a single layer of cube-shaped cells with clear boundaries between the cells, and narrow tubes with a very thin wall of flattened cells. Which part of the nephron are the narrow, thin-walled tubes?
jobs.authorBrief: Transverse section of kidney medulla as seen with a light microscope. Several wide circular tubes lined by one layer of cube-shaped cells with clear cell boundaries; between them, many narrow circular tubes with a very thin wall of flattened cells. Label one narrow tube "T". No part names on the drawing.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A glucose biosensor has the enzyme glucose oxidase immobilised on an electrode. The electrode gives an electric current that depends on the glucose concentration of the sample. A nurse calibrates the biosensor with glucose standards: 0.0 mmol dm⁻³ gives 0.0 μA, 2.5 mmol dm⁻³ gives 1.5 μA, 5.0 mmol dm⁻³ gives 3.0 μA, 7.5 mmol dm⁻³ gives 4.5 μA and 10.0 mmol dm⁻³ gives 6.0 μA. She then mixes 0.40 cm³ of a patient's blood plasma with 1.60 cm³ of buffer solution and tests the mixture. The current is 1.8 μA. Calculate the glucose concentration of the patient's blood plasma. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis: glucose concentration / mmol dm⁻³, 0 to 10.0. y-axis: current / μA, 0 to 6.0. Plot the five standards as crosses at (0.0, 0.0), (2.5, 1.5), (5.0, 3.0), (7.5, 4.5) and (10.0, 6.0) with a straight line of best fit through the origin. Do not mark the patient reading of 1.8 μA on the graph.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: Bean plants are grown with 12 hours of light (06:00 to 18:00) and 12 hours of darkness each day. Experiment 1: some plants are moved into continuous light at a constant temperature. For the next three days their stomata still widen and narrow, with the widest aperture about every 24 hours. Experiment 2: other plants are moved, at a constant temperature, to a new cycle with light from 18:00 to 06:00 and darkness from 06:00 to 18:00 each day. For the first two days their widest aperture is still at about midday. By the fifth day it is at about midnight. Which conclusion is supported by both experiments?
options: Stomata open only when light falls on the guard cells, so the rhythm depends on light alone.
The rhythm is produced inside the plant, and its timing can be reset by the cycle of light and dark.
The rhythm is produced inside the plant, and its timing cannot be changed by the cycle of light and dark.
The rhythm is caused by daily changes in the temperature around the leaves.
jobs.authorBrief: Graph 1 (experiment 1, continuous light): x-axis time / days 0 to 3, y-axis stomatal aperture / μm 0 to 10; a wave with a peak at about midday on each day; no dark periods shaded. Graph 2 (experiment 2): x-axis time / days 0 to 5, with the new dark periods (06:00 to 18:00) shaded; peaks at about midday on days 1 and 2, moving later on days 3 and 4, and at about midnight on day 5. No text giving a conclusion.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: In a normal guard cell, the cell wall next to the pore is thicker and less elastic than the outer wall, and the cellulose microfibrils in the wall are arranged in hoops around the cell. A mutant plant has guard cells with walls of the same thickness all round and cellulose microfibrils arranged at random. In the light, the mutant guard cells become turgid in the same way as normal guard cells. Which statement predicts what happens to the stomata of the mutant plant in the light?
options: The pores open wider than normal, because walls of equal thickness can stretch evenly in all directions.
The pores open normally, because opening depends only on the guard cells taking up water.
The pores close, because turgid guard cells always press against each other.
The guard cells swell, but they do not bend apart much, so the pores stay narrow.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a pair of kidney-shaped normal guard cells in surface view around a pore, with chloroplasts. Show the wall next to the pore thicker than the outer wall. Draw cellulose microfibrils as hoops running round each guard cell. Labels: guard cell, pore, thick inner wall, thin outer wall, cellulose microfibrils. Draw only normal guard cells, not the mutant cells.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A drug blocks the voltage-gated sodium ion channels in the sensory neurone that leads from a taste bud. It has no effect on the chemoreceptor cells. A salty solution is then placed on the tongue. Each option gives three answers in this order: (1) Does the chemoreceptor cell release neurotransmitter? (2) Is the membrane of the sensory neurone depolarised? (3) Are action potentials produced in the sensory neurone? Which option is correct?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a section through a taste bud in the tongue epithelium: a taste pore at the top, several chemoreceptor cells with microvilli projecting into the pore, supporting cells between them, and a sensory neurone ending that forms synapses at the base of the chemoreceptor cells. Labels: taste pore, microvilli, chemoreceptor cell, supporting cell, sensory neurone. Do not draw or label ion channels.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: In a normal action potential in an axon, the membrane potential rises from −70 mV to +35 mV in about 0.5 ms and then returns to below −70 mV within about 1.5 ms. A toxin stops voltage-gated potassium ion channels from opening, but has no effect on any other channels or on the sodium–potassium pump. Which statement predicts the action potential in an axon treated with the toxin?
options: No depolarisation happens, because potassium ions are needed to make the inside of the axon positive.
Depolarisation happens as normal, and the membrane repolarises faster than normal because no potassium ions leave.
Depolarisation happens as normal, but the membrane stays depolarised for much longer before it returns to the resting potential.
Depolarisation and repolarisation happen as normal, but the membrane potential does not go below −70 mV afterwards.
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis: time / ms, 0 to 4. y-axis: membrane potential / mV, −90 to +50. Resting level −70 mV; the trace rises to +35 mV at about 0.5 ms, falls below −70 mV to about −80 mV by about 1.5 ms, then returns to −70 mV by about 3 ms. Draw only this normal trace; do not draw a trace for the toxin-treated axon.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: An electron micrograph shows a transverse section (cross-section) through a myofibril from a relaxed striated muscle. In this section the thick filaments form a regular hexagonal pattern, and each thick filament is surrounded by six thin filaments. Through which region of the sarcomere did the section pass?
options: the part of the A band on either side of the H zone
jobs.authorBrief: Transverse section of part of one myofibril as seen in an electron micrograph. About seven large dots (thick filaments) in a hexagonal lattice; each large dot surrounded by six small dots (thin filaments), small dots shared between neighbouring large dots. Labels: "thick filament", "thin filament". Scale bar 50 nm. Do not name or label any band or zone of the sarcomere.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: In one myofibril every thick filament is 1.60 μm long, and every thin filament reaches 1.00 μm from the Z line to which it is attached. During a contraction, a sarcomere in this myofibril shortens from 2.40 μm to 2.10 μm. Which row shows the width of the H zone before and after the contraction and the width of the A band after the contraction?
options: H zone before: 0.20 μm; H zone after: 0.05 μm; A band after: 1.60 μm
H zone before: 0.40 μm; H zone after: 0.10 μm; A band after: 1.30 μm
H zone before: 0.80 μm; H zone after: 0.50 μm; A band after: 1.60 μm
H zone before: 0.40 μm; H zone after: 0.10 μm; A band after: 1.60 μm
jobs.authorBrief: One relaxed sarcomere drawn to scale, 2.40 μm between two Z lines (label "2.40 μm"). Thin filaments attached to each Z line, one labelled "1.00 μm". Thick filaments centred between the Z lines, one labelled "1.60 μm". Label "Z line" on both ends, "thick filament" and "thin filament". Do not label any band, the H zone or the M line, and show no band widths.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: The six chromosomes in a body cell of a diploid plant (2n = 6) are described below. The cell has not yet replicated its DNA. A capital letter shows one allele of a gene and a small letter shows the other allele. Chromosome 1: length 6.0 μm; centromere near the middle; flower colour allele F; stem height allele H. Chromosome 2: length 4.0 μm; centromere near one end; leaf shape allele L; seed coat colour allele c. Chromosome 3: length 6.0 μm; centromere near the middle; flower colour allele f; stem height allele H. Chromosome 4: length 4.0 μm; centromere near one end; root length allele R; petal number allele P. Chromosome 5: length 4.0 μm; centromere near one end; leaf shape allele l; seed coat colour allele C. Chromosome 6: length 4.0 μm; centromere near one end; root length allele R; petal number allele P. Which chromosomes form homologous pairs?
options: only 1 and 3, and 2 and 5, are pairs
jobs.authorBrief: Six single-chromatid chromosomes drawn side by side in number order 1-6, NOT grouped into pairs. Chromosomes 1 and 3: 6.0 μm, centromere near the middle. Chromosomes 2, 4, 5 and 6: 4.0 μm, centromere near one end. Mark two loci on each with the allele letters from the table (1: F, H; 2: L, c; 3: f, H; 4: R, P; 5: l, C; 6: R, P) and a key naming the genes (flower colour, stem height, leaf shape, seed coat colour, root length, petal number). Scale bar 1 μm.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A squash of testis tissue from an insect species with a diploid number of 8 chromosomes is stained and viewed with a light microscope. In one cell, the chromosomes are in two separate groups moving towards opposite ends of the cell. Each group contains 4 chromosomes, and each of these chromosomes still consists of two chromatids. Which stage of division is this cell in?
jobs.authorBrief: An animal cell with a spindle. Two groups of 4 chromosomes, one group partway towards each pole; the 4 chromosomes in a group are of 4 different lengths, and the two groups match each other in sizes. Each chromosome drawn as two chromatids attached at one centromere, with a spindle fibre attached at the centromere. No nuclear envelope. Do not label the stage.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: In a species of flowering plant, petal colour is made in two steps. Enzyme A, coded for by the dominant allele A, converts a colourless substance into a pink pigment. Enzyme D, coded for by the dominant allele D, converts the pink pigment into a purple pigment. The recessive alleles a and d code for non-functional enzymes. Petals with no pigment are white. The two genes are on different chromosomes. A plant with genotype AaDd is crossed with a plant with genotype Aadd. What is the expected ratio of phenotypes among the offspring?
jobs.authorBrief: Horizontal flowchart: box "colourless substance" -> arrow labelled "enzyme A (coded for by allele A)" -> box "pink pigment" -> arrow labelled "enzyme D (coded for by allele D)" -> box "purple pigment". No genotypes, no ratios.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: In pea plants, part of the pathway that makes gibberellins is GA12 → GA20 → GA1, and each arrow is a step catalysed by a different enzyme. A student grows dwarf pea plants with genotype le le and tall plants with genotype Le Le. She treats groups of le le seedlings in different ways and measures the mean internode length after 3 weeks. Results: Le Le, untreated: 62 mm; le le, untreated: 18 mm; le le, treated with GA20: 19 mm; le le, treated with GA1: 60 mm. Which conclusion is supported by these results?
options: The le allele codes for a non-functional form of the enzyme that converts GA20 into GA1.
The le allele codes for a non-functional form of the enzyme that converts GA12 into GA20.
Plants with genotype le le make GA1 normally, but their stem cells cannot respond to it.
GA20 is the gibberellin that causes internode elongation, and plants with genotype le le cannot make it.
jobs.authorBrief: Horizontal flowchart of three boxes: "GA12" -> "GA20" -> "GA1". Each arrow labelled "enzyme". Do not mark any step as blocked and do not label any allele.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: In the bacterium Escherichia coli, the lac operon contains a promoter, an operator and three structural genes: lacZ, lacY and lacA. A regulatory gene, lacI, lies outside the operon. When lactose is absent, the structural genes are not transcribed. When lactose is present, they are transcribed. Which statement explains why the structural genes are transcribed when lactose is present?
options: Lactose binds to the operator, so the repressor protein cannot bind there.
Lactose binds to the promoter, so RNA polymerase can attach to the DNA there.
Lactose binds to the repressor protein and changes its shape, so the repressor can no longer bind to the operator.
Lactose binds to RNA polymerase, so RNA polymerase binds to the operator instead of the promoter.
jobs.authorBrief: One horizontal DNA strip divided into labelled blocks from left to right: "lacI (regulatory gene)", a short gap, "promoter", "operator", "lacZ", "lacY", "lacA". Bracket under promoter to lacA labelled "lac operon". No proteins, no lactose, no arrows showing binding.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A population of a stick insect lives on an island. A bird that feeds mainly on large stick insects arrives on the island. Over the next 50 generations, the mean body length of the stick insects falls from 62 mm to 51 mm, and the spread of body lengths around the mean stays about the same. Which row describes the type of selection and the stick insects that it favoured?
options: directional selection; stick insects with shorter bodies
directional selection; stick insects with longer bodies
stabilising selection; stick insects with body lengths close to the mean
disruptive selection; stick insects with the shortest and the longest bodies
jobs.authorBrief: Line graph. x-axis: body length / mm, 30 to 80. y-axis: number of stick insects (no scale needed). Curve labelled "start": symmetrical bell shape with its peak at 62 mm. Curve labelled "after 50 generations": the same height and width, with its peak at 51 mm. No arrows and no label naming a type of selection.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A single-celled organism lives in a pond. Its DNA is in a nucleus. It has chloroplasts and photosynthesises, it has no cell wall, and it swims using a flagellum. Which kingdom does it belong to?
jobs.authorBrief: Simple labelled line drawing of one elongated cell, about 50 μm long (add a 10 μm scale bar). Labels: nucleus, chloroplast (several oval chloroplasts), cell surface membrane, flagellum (one long flagellum at the front end). Draw a single outer line only, with no cell wall. Do not name the kingdom.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A team estimates the percentage cover of a sedge (a grass-like plant) in a 50 m by 30 m area of wet grassland. About one-fifth of the area is muddy, and the sedge grows mainly in these muddy parts. The team places 40 quadrats at coordinates from a random number generator. When a coordinate falls in a muddy part, the team does not use it and generates a new coordinate instead. Which statement about their estimate of sedge cover is correct?
options: The estimate is likely to be too low, because the parts of the area where the sedge grows are not sampled.
The estimate is not biased, because every coordinate still came from a random number generator.
The estimate is likely to be too high, because more of the quadrats are placed in the dry parts of the area.
The estimate is less precise but not biased, because the number of quadrats is still 40.
jobs.authorBrief: Plan view of a 50 m by 30 m rectangle with labelled x-axis (0-50 m) and y-axis (0-30 m) grid lines every 5 m. Three or four irregular shaded patches labelled "muddy ground" covering about one-fifth of the area. A key: shaded = muddy ground. Do not mark quadrat positions or any sedge.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A large tree stands in an open grassy area. The ground under the tree is heavily shaded, and the shade becomes less with distance from the trunk. A student wants to find out how the percentage cover of each plant species changes with distance from the trunk out into the open grass. Which method should she use?
options: Place frame quadrats at random coordinates across the whole area around the tree.
Lay a tape from the trunk out into the open grass and place a quadrat at regular intervals along it, recording the percentage cover of each species.
Use mark-release-recapture to estimate the number of plants of each species.
Lay a tape from the trunk out into the open grass and record each species that touches the tape.
jobs.authorBrief: Side view of one large tree with a wide crown standing on flat grassland. Shade on the ground drawn as a darker band under the crown, fading with distance from the trunk. Label "trunk", "shaded ground" and "open grass". Add a scale bar of 5 m. Do not draw any tape, line or quadrats.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student measures soil water content and counts the plants of one species of rush in 8 quadrats. Quadrat 1: 12%, 4 plants. Quadrat 2: 18%, 9 plants. Quadrat 3: 25%, 7 plants. Quadrat 4: 31%, 15 plants. Quadrat 5: 9%, 6 plants. Quadrat 6: 22%, 11 plants. Quadrat 7: 35%, 13 plants. Quadrat 8: 15%, 3 plants. She uses Spearman's rank correlation, rs = 1 − (6 × Σd²) / (n(n² − 1)). The critical values of rs at p = 0.05 are 0.886 (n = 6), 0.786 (n = 7), 0.738 (n = 8), 0.700 (n = 9) and 0.648 (n = 10). Which row gives the value of rs, to 3 decimal places, and a correct conclusion?
options: \(r_s = 0.190\); there is no significant correlation between soil water content and the number of plants.
\(r_s = 0.810\); there is no significant correlation, because 0.810 is greater than the critical value.
\(r_s = 0.810\); there is a significant positive correlation, so a higher soil water content causes more rush plants to grow.
\(r_s = 0.810\); there is a significant positive correlation between soil water content and the number of plants.
jobs.authorBrief: Scatter graph. x-axis "soil water content / %", 0 to 40, grid every 5. y-axis "number of plants", 0 to 16, grid every 2. Plot eight crosses: (12, 4), (18, 9), (25, 7), (31, 15), (9, 6), (22, 11), (35, 13), (15, 3). No line of best fit and no value of the correlation coefficient.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A gene is cut out of donor DNA using two different restriction endonucleases, X and Y. Enzyme X cuts at one end of the gene and enzyme Y at the other end. The sticky ends made by X are not complementary to those made by Y. A plasmid is cut with the same two enzymes at two sites close together, and the short piece of DNA between the sites is removed. Which is an advantage of using two different enzymes instead of one enzyme that cuts at both ends of the gene?
options: Every bacterium that is mixed with the plasmids will take up a recombinant plasmid.
Each enzyme cuts the gene into shorter pieces, which are easier to insert into the plasmid.
The two ends of the cut plasmid become complementary to each other, so the plasmid closes around the gene faster.
The cut plasmid cannot join back into a circle without the gene, and the gene can fit into the plasmid in only one orientation.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a circular plasmid with two restriction sites labelled X and Y about 20° apart on the circle; show the short piece between them as removed (dashed). Beside it draw a linear double-stranded gene fragment whose left end is labelled "X sticky end" and right end "Y sticky end", with the two sticky-end shapes drawn differently. No arrows showing the result of ligation.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A plasmid carries a gene for resistance to the antibiotic ampicillin and a gene for green fluorescent protein (GFP). The only restriction site used lies in the middle of the GFP gene. Scientists cut the plasmids at this site, mix them with a cut human gene and DNA ligase, and then mix the plasmids with bacteria. The bacteria are grown on agar containing ampicillin and looked at under blue light. Some colonies glow green and some colonies do not glow. Which colonies contain bacteria that have taken up a plasmid with the human gene in it?
options: the colonies that glow, because the glow shows that the human gene is being expressed
the colonies that do not glow, because the human gene has split the GFP gene so no working GFP is made
all the colonies, because every bacterium that grows on ampicillin has the human gene
none of the colonies, because a plasmid with the human gene in it no longer gives resistance to ampicillin
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a circular plasmid. Label one arc "ampicillin-resistance gene" and a separate arc "GFP gene". Mark one restriction site with a short line and the label "restriction site", placed part-way along the GFP gene arc as the stem describes. No inserted gene and no colonies drawn.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A tube contains 80 copies of a target DNA sequence in 50 μl of PCR mixture. The PCR runs for 18 cycles. Then 1 μl of the 50 μl of product is moved into a second tube of fresh PCR mixture, and this tube runs for a further 12 cycles. Assume that the number of copies of the target sequence doubles in every cycle. Calculate the number of copies of the target sequence in the second tube at the end. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Box 1: "Tube 1: 80 copies of target, 50 μl mixture" → arrow labelled "18 cycles" → Box 2: "Tube 1 product". Arrow labelled "1 μl moved" → Box 3: "Tube 2: fresh PCR mixture" → arrow labelled "12 cycles" → Box 4: "Tube 2 product: ? copies". No numbers of copies other than 80.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A DNA ladder and a sample are run on the same gel. The ladder gives these results: 3200 bp at 10 mm from the well, 1600 bp at 18 mm, 800 bp at 26 mm, 400 bp at 34 mm and 200 bp at 42 mm. In this gel, the distance moved falls by the same amount each time the fragment length doubles. The sample gives one band, X, 30 mm from the well. Estimate the length of the fragment in band X. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a vertical agarose gel with two wells at the top. Lane 1 (ladder): five bands at 10, 18, 26, 34 and 42 mm from the well, labelled 3200, 1600, 800, 400 and 200 bp. Lane 2 (sample): one band labelled X at 30 mm from the well. Add a mm scale beside the gel. Do not label X with a length.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student investigates the effect of copper sulfate on root growth in cress seedlings. She has a stock solution of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ copper sulfate. She needs solutions of 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001 and 0.00001 mol dm⁻³, and makes them by serial dilution in clean test-tubes, each new solution from the one before. Which step does she repeat to make each new solution?
options: Transfer 1 cm³ of the previous solution into 10 cm³ of distilled water and mix.
Transfer 1 cm³ of the previous solution into 9 cm³ of distilled water and mix.
Transfer 2 cm³ of the previous solution into 8 cm³ of distilled water and mix.
Transfer 9 cm³ of the previous solution into 1 cm³ of distilled water and mix.
jobs.authorBrief: Draw five test-tubes in a row. Label them, left to right: stock 0.1 mol dm⁻³, 0.01 mol dm⁻³, 0.001 mol dm⁻³, 0.0001 mol dm⁻³, 0.00001 mol dm⁻³ (copper sulfate). Draw one curved arrow from each tube to the next, with no volumes written on the arrows or tubes.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem: A student uses a simple respirometer to measure the rate of oxygen uptake by germinating wheat grains. The grains sit on a gauze platform above soda lime, which absorbs carbon dioxide, in a boiling tube. The tube is joined to a capillary tube that contains a drop of coloured liquid, and a side tube with a screw clip can be opened to the air. The steps of her method are listed in random order. P: Put the tube into a water-bath at 25 °C with the screw clip open and leave it for 10 minutes. Q: Close the screw clip and start the stopwatch. R: Place 10 g of germinating wheat grains on the gauze above 5 g of soda lime and connect the tube to the capillary tube. S: Record the position of the coloured liquid on the scale every 2 minutes for 20 minutes. What is the correct order of the steps?
jobs.authorBrief: Draw a boiling tube in a water-bath. Inside: soda lime at the bottom, a wire-gauze platform, germinating wheat grains on the platform. A bung carries (1) a bent capillary tube with a millimetre scale and a drop of coloured liquid, and (2) a short side tube with rubber tubing and a screw clip. Label: soda lime, gauze, germinating wheat grains, capillary tube, scale, coloured liquid, screw clip, water-bath. Do not show the clip as open or closed.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem:
A student measures the shell length of 30 periwinkles (small sea snails) on each of three rocky shores, P, Q and R. She calculates the mean shell length and the standard error (SE) of the mean for each shore. She plots the means as a bar chart with error bars of ±2 SE.
Shore | mean shell length / mm | SE / mm
P | 14.2 | 0.4
Q | 15.3 | 0.3
R | 16.4 | 0.5
Which conclusion about the differences between the mean shell lengths is correct?
options: Only the difference between shores P and R is likely to be significant.
The differences between all three pairs of shores are likely to be significant.
Only the differences between P and Q and between Q and R are likely to be significant.
None of the differences is likely to be significant, because the means differ by less than 2.5 mm.
jobs.authorBrief: Vertical bar chart. x-axis: shore (P, Q, R). y-axis: mean shell length / mm, from 12 to 18. Bar heights 14.2, 15.3 and 16.4 mm. Error bars show ±2 SE: P from 13.4 to 15.0, Q from 14.7 to 15.9, R from 15.4 to 17.4 mm. No labels saying which bars overlap.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem:
Beads of alginate that contain the alga Chlorella are placed in buffered solutions with different concentrations of sodium hydrogencarbonate, a source of carbon dioxide. A student measures the rate of oxygen production by the beads at each concentration. All other conditions are kept constant.
Hydrogencarbonate concentration / mmol dm⁻³ | rate of oxygen production / μmol h⁻¹
0 | 0.3
2 | 2.6
4 | 4.7
6 | 5.5
8 | 5.6
10 | 5.6
In a second test at 8 mmol dm⁻³, a brighter light increases the rate further.
Which statement explains why the rate levels off at high hydrogencarbonate concentrations?
options: Light intensity becomes the limiting factor, so the light-dependent reactions cannot supply ATP and reduced NADP any faster for the reduction of GP to TP.
Carbon dioxide is still the limiting factor, because more carbon dioxide is needed for the photolysis of water.
The high hydrogencarbonate concentration denatures rubisco, so no more RuBP can be combined with carbon dioxide.
All the RuBP in the chloroplasts has been used up and cannot be made again, so the Calvin cycle stops.
jobs.authorBrief: Line graph. x-axis: hydrogencarbonate concentration / mmol dm⁻³, 0 to 10. y-axis: rate of oxygen production / μmol h⁻¹, 0 to 6. Plot points (0, 0.3), (2, 2.6), (4, 4.7), (6, 5.5), (8, 5.6), (10, 5.6) joined by straight lines. No annotations.

jobs.subject: biology
jobs.stem:
A student measures the rate at which the enzyme urease breaks down urea at five urea concentrations, with and without a fixed concentration of an inhibitor.
Urea concentration / mmol dm⁻³ | rate without inhibitor / μmol min⁻¹ | rate with inhibitor / μmol min⁻¹
5 | 12.0 | 4.8
10 | 19.2 | 8.7
20 | 27.4 | 14.8
40 | 34.9 | 22.6
80 | 40.4 | 30.7
She concludes that the inhibitor is a competitive inhibitor.
Which prediction follows from this conclusion?
options: At 80 mmol dm⁻³ urea, doubling the concentration of the inhibitor will increase the rate of reaction.
At 320 mmol dm⁻³ urea, the difference between the two rates will be larger than at 80 mmol dm⁻³.
At 320 mmol dm⁻³ urea, the difference between the two rates will be smaller than at 80 mmol dm⁻³.
At 320 mmol dm⁻³ urea, the rate without the inhibitor will be about four times the rate at 80 mmol dm⁻³.
jobs.authorBrief: Line graph. x-axis: urea concentration / mmol dm⁻³, 0 to 80. y-axis: rate / μmol min⁻¹, 0 to 45. Curve 1 (no inhibitor): (5, 12.0), (10, 19.2), (20, 27.4), (40, 34.9), (80, 40.4). Curve 2 (with inhibitor): (5, 4.8), (10, 8.7), (20, 14.8), (40, 22.6), (80, 30.7). Smooth curves through the points, a key for the two curves, no other labels.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student uses an oscilloscope to measure the alternating current in a resistor of resistance 47 Ω. She connects the oscilloscope across the resistor. The Y-gain is set to 0.50 V per division. The trace is a sine wave, and its height from the bottom of a trough to the top of a crest is 4.4 divisions. Calculate the root-mean-square (r.m.s.) current in the resistor. Give your answer to 2 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: Oscilloscope screen of 10 horizontal by 8 vertical divisions, labelled "Y-gain 0.50 V / div". A sine wave centred on the middle horizontal line, about two cycles across the screen, with each crest 2.2 divisions above and each trough 2.2 divisions below the centre line (crest-to-trough height 4.4 divisions). Show no current values.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A motion sensor lies on the floor and faces upwards. A small toy parachute is released above it and falls towards the sensor. A data logger plots a graph of the distance between the parachute and the sensor against time. The graph curves at first, and then becomes a straight line that slopes downwards until the parachute is close to the sensor. How should the student find the terminal speed of the parachute from the graph?
options: Find the magnitude of the gradient of the straight part of the graph.
Find the magnitude of the gradient at the start of the graph.
Find the area between the straight part of the graph and the time axis.
Divide the starting distance by the total time of the fall.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: distance / m from 0 to 2.0 on the y-axis, time / s from 0 to 3.0 on the x-axis. The line starts at 2.0 m at t = 0 with a horizontal tangent, curves downwards and becomes steeper, then from about t = 0.8 s continues as a straight line sloping down to 0.20 m at about t = 2.6 s, where the recorded data end. No gradient values and no labels naming any part of the graph.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student investigates how the frequency f of the note from a struck metal rod depends on the length L of the rod. She suggests that f = aLⁿ, where a and n are constants. Her rods have lengths from 0.20 m to 0.50 m. She plots a graph of lg (f / Hz) against lg (L / m), and the axes do not start at zero. The line of best fit is straight and passes through the points (−0.700, 3.750) and (−0.300, 2.950), written as (lg (L / m), lg (f / Hz)). Calculate the value of a. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
jobs.authorBrief: x-axis lg (L / m) from −0.75 to −0.25; y-axis lg (f / Hz) from 2.80 to 3.90; neither axis starts at zero. A straight line of best fit through two points marked with crosses and labelled with their coordinates, (−0.700, 3.750) and (−0.300, 2.950). Do not show the y-intercept or write the gradient.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student investigates how the pressure p measured by a sensor depends on the depth h of the sensor below the surface of a liquid. The results (h / m, p / kPa) are: (0.20, 1.9), (0.40, 3.8), (0.60, 5.6), (0.80, 7.6), (1.00, 9.4). The student plots p against h. The error bars show an uncertainty of ±0.2 kPa in each value of p. Each option describes a straight line by the points where it crosses h = 0.20 m and h = 1.00 m. Which line could be drawn as the worst acceptable line?
options: from (0.20 m, 1.6 kPa) to (1.00 m, 9.7 kPa)
from (0.20 m, 1.9 kPa) to (1.00 m, 9.4 kPa)
from (0.20 m, 2.1 kPa) to (1.00 m, 9.6 kPa)
from (0.20 m, 1.7 kPa) to (1.00 m, 9.6 kPa)
jobs.authorBrief: Graph grid with h / m on the x-axis from 0 to 1.00 (0.10 m per large square) and p / kPa on the y-axis from 0 to 10.0 (1.0 kPa per large square). Plot the five points (0.20, 1.9), (0.40, 3.8), (0.60, 5.6), (0.80, 7.6), (1.00, 9.4) as small crosses, each with a vertical error bar of ±0.2 kPa. Draw no lines on the graph.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student investigates resonance in a tube that is closed at one end. For each sound frequency f, the student finds the shortest length l of the air column that gives resonance. It is suggested that l = v/(4f) − e, where v is the speed of sound in air and e is a constant. The student plots a graph with 1/f on the y-axis and l on the x-axis. Which row gives the gradient and the y-intercept of the line?
jobs.authorBrief: A vertical glass tube standing in water so that the air column above the water surface has length l (double-headed arrow labelled l from the water surface to the open top). A small loudspeaker connected to a signal generator labelled "frequency f" is held just above the open top of the tube. No numerical values.

jobs.subject: physics
jobs.stem: A student measures the resistance R of a coil of copper wire at different temperatures θ and plots a graph of R against θ. The θ-axis starts at 20 °C. The line of best fit passes through (20 °C, 5.60 Ω) and (100 °C, 9.20 Ω). The worst acceptable line passes through (20 °C, 5.90 Ω) and (100 °C, 9.02 Ω). Calculate the absolute uncertainty in the y-intercept of the line of best fit.
jobs.authorBrief: Axes: θ / °C on the x-axis from 20 to 100 (the y-axis is drawn at θ = 20 °C, a false origin); R / Ω on the y-axis from 4.0 to 10.0. Solid straight line labelled "best fit" from (20, 5.60) to (100, 9.20). Dashed straight line labelled "worst acceptable" from (20, 5.90) to (100, 9.02). Mark the four end points with small dots and their coordinates. Do not mark any intercept values.
